entries.wohChoice: chapter-title 'Isaiah 6 - The throne-room vision and the prophet's commission' (the Translator's descriptive long-form title, ratified). Divine-name house-style for the book, established here: the Tetragrammaton יְהוָה is rendered 'YHWH' (ISA-6:3, 6:5, 6:12), matching the corpus-wide YHWH convention; the bare divine title אֲדֹנָי is rendered 'the Lord' (ISA-6:1, 6:8, 6:11) and kept typographically and lexically distinct from YHWH; the seraphim are transliterated; the first-person-plural divine speech is preserved literally without committing the text to a reading.
entries.rationale: This meta-entry records the divine-name house-style Isaiah inherits from the established corpus convention and fixes for the book at its opening chapter. The Masoretic text of Isaiah 6 alternates deliberately between the Tetragrammaton יְהוָה (6:3, 6:5, 6:12) and the bare title אֲדֹנָי (6:1, 6:8, 6:11); the project renders the two distinctly - 'YHWH' for the Tetragrammaton and 'the Lord' for אֲדֹנָי - so the reader can see the source's own lexical alternation rather than the flattening 'the LORD / the Lord' English convention that masks it. No lens is carried in the title or the name-conventions: they are descriptive of the text and consistent with the corpus. The seraphim-transliteration and divine-plural-preservation decisions are given their own entries below and cross-referenced here only as house-style.

entries.lemma: ʾăḏōnāy (standalone divine title; not the compound אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה)
entries.partOfSpeech: divine title (noun, plural-of-majesty of אָדוֹן 'lord/master' with 1cs suffix, used absolutely of the deity)
entries.literal: my lords / the Lord
entries.standardEnglish: the Lord (ASV/JPS/NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: 'the Lord' - the standalone אֲדֹנָי title rendered as the ASV/JPS/NRSV standard, kept distinct from 'YHWH' (the corpus rendering of the Tetragrammaton) and from the compound 'Lord YHWH' (the Ezekiel/Genesis adonai-yhwh entries).
entries.rationale: The Masoretic text of Isaiah 6 opens and structures its call-narrative with the bare title אֲדֹנָי - at 6:1 (the vision), 6:8 (the commissioning voice), and 6:11 ('How long, O Lord?') - a genuine divine title (the plural-of-majesty of אָדוֹן 'lord, master') and not the Tetragrammaton, which appears separately at 6:3, 6:5, 6:12. No production-glossary entry governs bare אֲדֹנָי: the existing adonai-yhwh and adonai-yhwh-divine-name entries cover only the compound אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה and are scoped to Ezekiel and Genesis. The Editor renders 'the Lord' (the ASV/JPS/NRSV standard) rather than the escalation-option of reading אֲדֹנָי as a reverential substitution masking an original יהוה: some manuscripts and the tradition of the tiqqune sopherim show scribal sensitivity around the divine names in Isaiah 6, but the consonantal MT reads אֲדֹנָי and accuracy-before-lens forbids promoting a conjectured 'YHWH' into the text where the received text is unambiguous. Keeping 'the Lord' distinct from 'YHWH' preserves the source's own alternation of the two designations, which the throne-vision deploys pointedly.

entries.standardEnglish: a throne, high and lifted up (ASV); a high and lofty throne (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: the pair modifies the throne: 'a throne, high and lifted up' - the participles rām wᵉniśśāʾ read as attributive to כִּסֵּא (masc. sg., which they immediately follow and agree with), not as predicated of the seated Lord.
entries.rationale: The word-pair רָם וְנִשָּׂא stands directly after כִּסֵּא and agrees with it in gender and number, so the natural syntactic reading takes the throne, not the seated figure, as exalted - the rendering of ASV, JPS, and the major commentaries (Wildberger, Isaiah 1-12, 1991; Williamson, ICC Isaiah 6-12, 2018). The escalation-option that the pair describes the Lord draws on Isa 57:15, where רָם וְנִשָּׂא is applied to God ('the high and lofty One'), but that is a separate, independent construction and cannot govern the syntax here. The Editor ratifies the throne-attachment as the accuracy-first reading; the theological point that the exaltation of the throne connotes the exaltation of its occupant is a matter of sense, not syntax, and is left to the commentary rather than imposed on the line.

entries.strongs: H7757 (šûl)
entries.lemma: šûl (the hem/skirt/train of a garment), here suffixed שׁוּלָיו 'his hem(s)'
entries.literal: his skirts/hems (were) filling the temple
entries.standardEnglish: his train (JPS); the hem of his robe (NRSV); his train filled the temple (ASV)
entries.wohChoice: 'the hem of his robe filled the temple' - שׁוּל = the lower hem/skirt/train of a garment; the singular-collective English 'the hem of his robe' for the Hebrew plural שׁוּלָיו, the image being the robe's train flooding the sanctuary.
entries.rationale: שׁוּל denotes the lower hem, skirt, or train of a garment (BDB, HALOT), and the plural שׁוּלָיו pictures the trailing skirts of the enthroned figure's robe overspreading the sanctuary - a deliberately anthropomorphic and spatial image (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39, AB 19, 2000). The Editor keeps the accessible 'the hem of his robe' (with 'train' recorded as an equally defensible value) rather than the archaizing 'skirts'; no reading diverges from the standard scholarly sense. The point of interest for the vision - that a mere hem of the robe suffices to fill the whole hall, implying the immensity of the seated figure - is a matter of the image, developed in commentary, not a lexical divergence in the text.

entries.lemma: hêḵāl (temple; palace; great hall / nave)
entries.literal: the palace / temple / great hall
entries.standardEnglish: the temple (ASV/JPS/NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: 'the temple' - the standard rendering, with the palace / royal-audience-hall register of hêḵāl noted in commentary rather than surfaced in the line.
entries.rationale: hêḵāl (a loanword, ultimately Sumerian e-gal 'big house' via Akkadian ekallu 'palace') means both 'palace' and 'temple', and specifically the great hall or nave of the temple (BDB, HALOT). The Editor renders 'the temple', the standard value and the one the immediate context requires: the vision is set in the Jerusalem sanctuary (the year of Uzziah's death), and the altar of 6:6 (מִזְבֵּחַ) confirms the cultic setting. The palace / royal-audience-hall resonance - the enthroned sovereign holding court in his hall, which is where the throne-audience and the commissioning of a messenger belong - is genuine to the word and is WoH-salient, but rendering it 'palace' would over-specify against the temple setting the chapter builds; that register is therefore carried in the commentary, not the line.

entries.strongs: H8314 (śārāp̄); root H8313 (śārap̄ 'to burn')
entries.lemma: śārāp̄ / plural śᵉrāp̄îm (a class of winged throne-attendant), root śrp 'to burn'
entries.literal: burning ones
entries.standardEnglish: seraphim (ASV/JPS/NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: transliterate 'seraphim' - the winged throne-attendants of the vision; the root-sense 'burning ones' (śrp 'to burn') and the winged-attendant / uraeus iconographic background and the divine-council resonance are carried in commentary. The text does NOT render 'fiery serpents' in the throne-vision.
entries.rationale: śᵉrāp̄îm is the plural of śārāp̄, from the root śrp 'to burn', hence the literal 'burning ones'; in Isaiah 6 the word names six-winged attendants standing above the throne, calling the trishagion and mediating the coal-purification (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp). The Editor transliterates 'seraphim' - the standard scholarly rendering (ASV/JPS/NRSV) - because the term functions here as the proper name of a specific order of throne-beings, not as a live adjective; translating 'burning ones' would be defensible etymologically but would lose the recognizability of the class and is reserved for the commentary. The third escalation-option, 'fiery/flying serpents' (the śārāp̄ of Num 21:6, Deut 8:15, Isa 14:29, 30:6, and the winged-uraeus iconographic parallels discussed by Joines, JBL 86 [1967], and Wildberger), is deliberately DECLINED for the throne-vision: whatever the iconographic prehistory of the seraph-figure, the beings of Isaiah 6 have faces, feet, hands, and voices and act as courtiers, so 'serpents' would import a reading the scene does not support - an accuracy-before-lens ruling. The cross-corpus link to the Ezekiel-1 living-creatures and the Revelation-4 four-living-creatures who take up the same trishagion is developed in commentary and via the central merkavah-tradition entry.

entries.strongs: H3068 (YHWH); H6635 (ṣāḇāʾ, plural ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ)
entries.lemma: YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ ('YHWH of hosts/armies')
entries.partOfSpeech: divine name + noun in a genitival/appositional bond
entries.literal: YHWH of armies/hosts
entries.standardEnglish: the LORD of hosts (ASV/JPS); YHWH of hosts
entries.wohChoice: 'YHWH of hosts' - the standard rendering, retaining the corpus 'YHWH' house-style; the reading of צְבָאוֹת as the heavenly host / divine assembly (the armies of the assembly convened around the throne) is carried in commentary, not by altering the title.
entries.rationale: יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת, 'YHWH of hosts', is the throne-vision's governing divine title, recurring at 6:3 (the seraphim's ascription) and 6:5 (Isaiah's confession 'my eyes have seen the King, YHWH of hosts'). צָבָא is 'army, host', and the title's original reference is disputed - the armies of Israel, the astral bodies, or the heavenly army / divine council - with the assembly-of-heavenly-beings reading argued at length by Mullen (The Divine Council in Canaanite and Early Hebrew Literature, 1980) and F. M. Cross (Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic, 1973), who read ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ as YHWH's command of the heavenly host that constitutes the council. The Editor keeps the standard 'YHWH of hosts' in the text (accuracy-before-lens: the title is a fixed epithet and the divergent 'of the heavenly host/armies' would over-translate a frozen form) and confines the heavenly-host/assembly reading - a canon-salient site, since the throne is surrounded by attendant beings in this very vision - to the commentary. The rendering is the standard one and carries no lens; only the house-style 'YHWH' (for the Tetragrammaton) distinguishes it from the KJV/ASV 'the LORD of hosts'.

entries.strongs: H3519 (kāḇôḏ), root H3513 (kāḇēḏ 'be heavy'); H776 (ʾereṣ); H4393 (mᵉlōʾ)
entries.lemma: kāḇôḏ (glory / weight / radiant presence), here suffixed כְּבוֹדוֹ 'his glory'
entries.partOfSpeech: noun (with 3ms suffix), predicate of a verbless clause
entries.literal: the fullness of all the earth (is) his glory
entries.standardEnglish: the whole earth is full of his glory (ASV/JPS); the fullness of the whole earth is his glory
entries.wohChoice: 'the fullness of the whole earth is his glory' - the literal nominal-clause word order preserved (kᵉḇôḏô as predicate), with kᵉḇôḏô rendered 'his glory'; the physical-presence sense of kāḇôḏ (the weighty, radiant manifestation) and the cosmic scope of kol hā-ʾāreṣ ('the whole earth') carried in commentary. Distinct grammatical form from the construct kᵉḇôḏ-YHWH governed by the Ezekiel-scoped kavod-yhwh entry.
entries.rationale: כְּבוֹדוֹ is the suffixed form of כָּבוֹד ('glory'), from the root kbd 'to be heavy'; the term is the Hebrew Bible's technical word for the weighty, radiant, quasi-physical presence-manifestation of the deity (Ex 40:34-35; 1 Kgs 8:10-11; Ezek 1:28), a sense the central kavod-yhwh entry documents for the construct כְּבוֹד־יְהוָה in Ezekiel. That entry cannot govern here because the form differs: Isaiah has the suffixed predicate כְּבוֹדוֹ in a verbless clause, not the bound construct. The Editor preserves the draft's literal word order 'the fullness of the whole earth is his glory' - which keeps kᵉḇôḏô as the clause's predicate, a defensible construal of מְלֹא כָל־הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ alongside the smoother 'the whole earth is full of his glory' - and renders kol hā-ʾāreṣ 'the whole earth' in its cosmic scope (the standard reading here, over against the 'whole land' value the Gen-1-scoped eretz entry uses). The physical-presence, kavod-fills-space register (the same phenomenon Isaiah's smoke-filled house dramatizes) is the WoH-salient point and is developed in commentary; the text keeps the standard 'his glory', so the entry is direct.

entries.strongs: H520 (ʾammāh); H5592 (sap̄, plural sippîm)
entries.lemma: ʾammôṯ ha-sippîm (the posts/foundations of the thresholds)
entries.literal: the pivots/foundations of the thresholds/sills
entries.standardEnglish: the foundations of the thresholds (JPS); the posts of the door (ASV)
entries.wohChoice: 'the foundations of the thresholds' - ʾammôṯ as the sockets/foundations bearing the doorframe, sippîm as the thresholds/door-sills; the architectural element that shook at the seraph's voice.
entries.rationale: אַמָּה here is not 'cubit' but a structural member - the pivot, socket, or foundation on which the door-structure turns or rests - and סַף is the threshold or door-sill (BDB, HALOT); the pair names the load-bearing base of the doorway that trembles at the sound (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp). The Editor follows JPS 'the foundations of the thresholds' as the most transparent rendering, with 'the posts of the door' (ASV) and 'the door-pivots/sockets' recorded as defensible alternatives among which the sources do not decisively adjudicate. The decision is lexical-architectural and carries no lens; verse 4 is scene-setting (the shaking sanctuary and the filling smoke) and receives no separate commentary.

entries.strongs: H1820 (dāmāh II 'be cut off, cease, be ruined'); cf. H1826 (dāmam 'be silent')
entries.lemma: niḏmêṯî (Niphal 1cs; root ambiguous between dmh 'be ruined/undone' and dmm 'be silenced')
entries.literal: I am ruined / cut off / undone
entries.standardEnglish: I am undone (ASV); I am lost (NRSV/NJPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'I am undone' - the dmh 'be cut off / ruined / doomed' reading (the sense of imminent destruction on seeing the deity), with the competing dmm 'be silenced / struck dumb' reading noted in commentary.
entries.rationale: נִדְמֵיתִי is a genuine root-crux: it may derive from דמה 'to cease, be cut off, be ruined/destroyed' (BDB, HALOT), giving 'I am undone / ruined / doomed', or from דמם 'to be silent, be struck dumb', giving 'I am silenced'. The Editor renders 'I am undone', the majority scholarly and versional reading (ASV; JPS/NRSV 'I am lost'), because the following clause supplies the ground - 'for my eyes have seen the King' - which invokes the lethal danger of seeing the deity (Ex 33:20; Judg 13:22), a fear of destruction rather than of muteness. The 'struck dumb / silenced' reading is contextually attractive - it would chime with the 'unclean lips' motif that dominates Isaiah's confession and its coal-cure - and it is recorded in the commentary as a live alternative, but it is the minority reading and is not promoted into the text. The chosen rendering is the standard one; the entry is direct with the crux flagged.

entries.strongs: H4428 (meleḵ); H7200 (rāʾāh)
entries.lemma: ha-meleḵ ('the King', divine title in apposition to YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ)
entries.partOfSpeech: noun (definite), divine title, object of 'have seen'
entries.literal: for the King, YHWH of hosts, my eyes have seen
entries.standardEnglish: the King, the LORD of hosts (ASV/JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'the King, YHWH of hosts' - הַמֶּלֶךְ as a divine title in apposition to YHWH of hosts; the theological weight of physically seeing the enthroned deity (the danger behind Isaiah's 'woe') carried in commentary.
entries.rationale: הַמֶּלֶךְ 'the King' stands in apposition to יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת and is the object of רָאוּ עֵינָי 'my eyes have seen' - the enthroned figure of the vision is titled 'the King', a designation with royal-throne resonance that the whole scene (throne, hall, courtiers, audience) sustains (Wildberger; Williamson, ICC). The Editor renders the standard 'the King, YHWH of hosts'; no reading diverges from the versions. The salient point - that Isaiah's cry of woe is grounded in the peril of having physically seen the deity, against the tradition that no one sees God and lives (Ex 33:20; cf. Gen 32:31; Judg 13:22) - is a matter of the scene's theology and is developed in the commentary rather than surfaced by re-rendering the title.

entries.strongs: H7531 (riṣpāh); H4457 (melqāḥayim); H4196 (mizbēaḥ)
entries.lemma: riṣpāh (a live coal / hot glowing stone), taken with מֶלְקַחַיִם (tongs) from the מִזְבֵּחַ (altar)
entries.literal: a glowing/hot stone (a live coal)
entries.standardEnglish: a live coal (ASV/JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'a glowing coal' - riṣpāh as the live/glowing coal (or heated stone) lifted with tongs from the altar; the mouth-and-lip purification it effects in v7 carried in commentary.
entries.rationale: רִצְפָּה denotes a hot, glowing stone or live coal (BDB, HALOT; cf. the cognate sense of rṣp 'to set/join stones', and 1 Kgs 19:6 rᵉṣap̄îm 'hot stones/coals'), here taken from the altar with tongs (מֶלְקַחַיִם) - the seraph handles it with tongs precisely because it is too hot to hold. The Editor keeps the draft's 'glowing coal' (with 'live coal', ASV/JPS, and 'burning/hot stone' as equivalents), the standard rendering; no divergence from the versions. That the burning coal from the altar touches and purges the 'unclean lips' - fire as the agent of purification and consecration for speech - is the point of the scene and is developed in the commentary on vv 6-7.

entries.strongs: H5493 (sûr); H5771 (ʿāwōn); H2403 (ḥaṭṭāʾṯ); H3722 (kāp̄ar)
entries.lemma: tᵉḵuppār (Pual imperfect of kpr 'to atone, expiate, purge, cover'); with sār ʿăwōn 'iniquity is removed'
entries.literal: your iniquity is turned-aside, and your sin is atoned/purged/covered
entries.standardEnglish: thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged (ASV); your iniquity shall depart and your sin be purged away (JPS/NRSV); expiated (NJPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'your iniquity is removed, and your sin is atoned for' - sār ʿăwōn 'iniquity removed'; tᵉḵuppār (kpr) rendered 'atoned for' (with 'purged / wiped away' as equivalents), the ritual purgation the coal effects.
entries.rationale: The verse pairs two purgation-verbs: סָר (from סור 'to turn aside'), the iniquity 'is removed', and תְּכֻפָּר, a Pual of כפר, the sin 'is atoned/expiated/purged' - the standard priestly kpr vocabulary for the wiping-away or covering of sin (BDB, HALOT; the cover/wipe etymological debate is longstanding). The Editor renders 'your iniquity is removed, and your sin is atoned for' (with JPS/NJPS 'expiated' and ASV 'purged' as equivalents), the standard versional reading; no divergence. The scene's logic - that the altar-coal's touch performs on Isaiah's lips a cultic purgation the priesthood otherwise performs by blood and fire - is developed in the commentary on vv 6-7, not asserted by re-rendering the verb.

entries.source: הַשְׁמֵן לֵב־הָעָם הַזֶּה וְאָזְנָיו הַכְבֵּד וְעֵינָיו הָשַׁע
entries.translit: hašmēn lēḇ-hā-ʿām ha-zzeh wᵉ-ʾoznāyw haḵbēḏ wᵉ-ʿênāyw hāšaʿ
entries.strongs: H8080 (šāmēn 'be/grow fat'); H3513 (kāḇēḏ 'be heavy'); H8173 (šāʿaʿ 'smear over, be blinded'); H3820 (lēḇ)
entries.lemma: the hardening-commission imperatives: hašmēn 'make fat/dull', haḵbēḏ 'make heavy', hāšaʿ 'smear over / shut'
entries.literal: make fat the heart of this people, and make its ears heavy, and smear-over its eyes
entries.standardEnglish: Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes (ASV); Dull the mind of this people, stop up its ears, and seal its eyes (NJPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'Make the heart of this people fat, make its ears heavy, and smear over its eyes' - the purposive imperatives of hardening read at face value (the divinely-commanded non-comprehension), with the ironic/rhetorical and resultative construals carried in commentary. Pairs with the doubled-infinitive intensives of v9 governed by the central harbah-arbeh-doubled-infinitive-intensive entry.
entries.rationale: Verse 10 issues three causative imperatives - הַשְׁמֵן 'make fat/dull' (the heart), הַכְבֵּד 'make heavy' (the ears), הָשַׁע 'smear over / shut' (the eyes) - followed by the פֶּן 'lest' clause 'lest it see... and turn back and be healed'; grammatically these are imperatives addressed to the prophet, commissioning him to render the people insensible (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp; Williamson, ICC). The Editor renders them at face value as the purposive hardening-commission (ASV/JPS baseline), which is what the Hebrew says; the softening alternatives - the ironic/rhetorical reading (a bitter prediction of futile reception cast as command) and the resultative reading ('so that', foreseen outcome rather than intended purpose), together with the ancient tradition of easing the offense (the LXX recasts the imperatives as a resultative statement of fact, 'the heart of this people has grown dull', and the Targum paraphrases) - are theologically significant and are surfaced in the commentary, but they are not imposed on the line, since accuracy requires the imperatives to stand. The doubled-infinitive intensives of v9 ('hear indeed... see indeed') are handled by the central harbah-arbeh-doubled-infinitive-intensive entry, which already lists ISA-6:9. No lens is carried in the text.

entries.source: וְשָׁבָה וְהָיְתָה לְבָעֵר ... אֲשֶׁר בְּשַׁלֶּכֶת מַצֶּבֶת בָּם
entries.translit: wᵉšāḇāh wᵉhāyᵉṯāh lᵉḇāʿēr ... ʾăšer bᵉšalleḵeṯ maṣṣeḇeṯ bām
entries.strongs: H1197 (bāʿar 'burn, consume'); H4678 (maṣṣeḇeṯ 'stump, stock'); H7995 (šalleḵeṯ 'felling'); H424 (ʾēlāh 'terebinth'); H437 (ʾallôn 'oak')
entries.lemma: lᵉḇāʿēr 'to be burned/consumed' (bʿr); maṣṣeḇeṯ 'stump/stock' of a felled terebinth/oak
entries.literal: and it shall again be for burning ... whose stump/stock (remains) in them when felled
entries.standardEnglish: it shall be eaten up ... whose stock remaineth when they are felled (ASV); it shall be ravaged ... whose stump remains when it is felled (NRSV/NJPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'it too shall again be for burning ... like the terebinth and like the oak, whose stump remains in them when they are felled' - lᵉḇāʿēr rendered 'for burning' (the bʿr 'burn/consume' sense), maṣṣeḇeṯ as the tree-stump/stock left standing after felling (šalleḵeṯ).
entries.rationale: The verse turns on two lexical decisions: לְבָעֵר, from בער 'to burn, kindle, consume', which the Editor renders 'for burning' (with the extended 'to be consumed/ravaged', NRSV/NJPS, and the by-grazing sense 'be browsed' recorded as a minority botanical construal); and מַצֶּבֶת, the stump, stock, or standing-trunk of a felled tree (BDB, HALOT), pictured for the אֵלָה 'terebinth' and אַלּוֹן 'oak' left as a stump בְּשַׁלֶּכֶת 'when felled / in their felling'. The Editor follows the standard felled-tree image (ASV/NRSV/NJPS); the botanical pair terebinth/oak is rendered by its conventional values and receives no separate entry. The whole clause is the vehicle for the remnant-image that the following words (זֶרַע קֹדֶשׁ 'the holy seed') interpret, and that theology is developed in the commentary on 6:13; the renderings here are lexical and carry no lens.

entries.strongs: H2233 (zeraʿ); H6944 (qōḏeš); H4678 (maṣṣeḇeṯ, suffixed)
entries.lemma: zeraʿ qōḏeš ('holy seed') - the closing clause of Isa 6:13, subject to a text-critical minus in the Old Greek
entries.literal: a holy seed (is) its stump
entries.standardEnglish: the holy seed is the stock thereof (ASV); the holy seed is its stump (NRSV/NJPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'the holy seed is its stump' - the MT closing clause retained, rendering the remnant that survives the felling as a 'holy seed'; the LXX-minus of the whole clause and the remnant/regeneration reading flagged in commentary as a text-critical and interpretive matter, not resolved in the line.
entries.rationale: The Masoretic text closes 6:13 with זֶרַע קֹדֶשׁ מַצַּבְתָּהּ, 'a holy seed (is) its stump' - identifying the surviving stump of the felled tree with a consecrated remnant, the germ from which the people can regrow (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp; Williamson, ICC). The Editor retains the MT clause and its standard rendering; the significant text-critical fact - that the closing clause זֶרַע קֹדֶשׁ מַצַּבְתָּהּ is absent from the Old Greek (LXX), which many read as marking it a later, hope-bearing addition to an otherwise unrelieved oracle of devastation - is recorded in the commentary rather than acted on, since the received Hebrew text carries the clause and the project translates the MT. The remnant/holy-seed motif is theologically weighty and canon-adjacent (a preserved seed-line surviving catastrophe), and that reading is developed in the commentary; the text keeps the standard rendering and the entry is direct, with the LXX-minus disclosed for the reader's audit.

entries.strongs: H5650 (ʿeḇeḏ)
entries.lemma: ʿeḇeḏ 'servant', here suffixed עַבְדִּי 'my servant' (Isa 53:11); the un-named protagonist of the whole fourth Servant Song
entries.partOfSpeech: noun (with 1cs suffix), divine designation of the song's protagonist
entries.literal: my servant
entries.standardEnglish: my servant (ASV/JPS/NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: 'my servant' / 'he' / 'him' - the servant language rendered plainly and the figure left un-identified in the text; the corporate-Israel, individual-prophet, messianic, and comparative dying-and-vindicated-figure readings all confined to commentary as hedged comparative/critical layers, with NO Wheel of Heaven identification of the servant asserted in the line.
entries.rationale: עַבְדִּי 'my servant' is grammatically explicit at 53:11 and names the figure - un-identified - who runs through the whole fourth Servant Song; 'my servant' is the standard rendering (ASV/JPS/NRSV) and carries no lens. The referent is the single most contested question in the study of the chapter: the mainstream Jewish reading takes the servant as corporate Israel or a faithful remnant (grounded in Isa 49:3 'you are my servant, Israel', and the medieval exegetes); a second reading takes an individual - a suffering prophet or Deutero-Isaiah himself, since Duhm's isolation of the four Servant Songs; the Christian reading takes an individual messiah who suffers vicariously, the reading the New Testament develops (Acts 8:32-35; 1 Pet 2:22-25); and some scholarship notes a broader comparative resonance with the righteous-sufferer-vindicated pattern. The Hebrew names no referent, and accuracy-before-lens forbids resolving it in the line: per the house register these readings are set out in commentary as comparative and critical layers, all hedged, and the chapter's Wheel of Heaven value lies in that critical/comparative apparatus, not in any direct-canon identification of the servant. North (The Suffering Servant in Deutero-Isaiah) surveys the interpretive history; this entry records the deliberate non-identification as the governing lens-discipline decision for the chapter.

entries.strongs: H2490 (ḥālal 'pierce, wound, bore through; profane')
entries.lemma: mᵉḥōlāl (Pual participle of ḥll I 'pierce, wound, slay')
entries.literal: pierced / wounded through
entries.standardEnglish: wounded (ASV/KJV/NRSV); pierced (NIV/ESV)
entries.wohChoice: 'pierced' - the Pual of ḥll I 'to pierce, bore through, fatally wound', with 'wounded' (ASV/NRSV) recorded as an equivalent; the minority derivation from ḥll II 'profane, defile' is declined.
entries.rationale: מְחֹלָל is a Pual participle whose root is disputed between ḥll I 'to pierce, bore through, wound fatally' (BDB, HALOT) and ḥll II 'to profane, defile'; the overwhelming majority of lexica, versions, and commentators take ḥll I, giving 'pierced' or 'wounded' (Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 40-55, AB 19A, 2002; Goldingay & Payne, ICC Isaiah 40-55). The translation renders 'pierced', a defensible strong gloss of the core sense (bore/run through), with the ASV/NRSV 'wounded' noted as equivalent; the choice matches scholarly consensus and carries no lens, so the entry is direct with the ḥll I/II root-crux flagged. The parallel מְדֻכָּא 'crushed' (from dkʾ) confirms the register of violent affliction, and the causal min governing both ('because of our transgressions / iniquities') is a matter of the following words, not this participle.

entries.strongs: H5375 (nāśāʾ 'lift, bear, carry'); H5445 (sāḇal 'bear a load, carry')
entries.lemma: the bearing-pair nāśāʾ 'bore' and sāḇal 'carried', of the servant carrying others' sickness/pain/iniquity/sin (Isa 53:4, 53:11, 53:12)
entries.partOfSpeech: two verbs (qal), the song's vicarious-bearing vocabulary
entries.literal: he lifted/bore … he carried
entries.standardEnglish: he bore / he carried (ASV/JPS/NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: 'bore' / 'carried' - the bearing-verbs rendered plainly; the substitutionary / vicarious-atonement sense (one bearing what belongs to others) developed as a hedged reading in commentary, not overloaded onto the verbs.
entries.rationale: נָשָׂא 'lift, bear, carry away' (H5375) and סָבַל 'bear a load, carry' (H5445) are the song's recurring bearing-verbs: the servant 'bore' (nāśāʾ) our sicknesses and 'carried' (sāḇal) our pains (53:4), 'carries' (sāḇal) their iniquities (53:11), and 'bore' (nāśāʾ) the sin of many (53:12). Each rendering is the standard versional value (ASV/JPS/NRSV) and carries no lens; the entry is direct. The theological weight these verbs bear in later interpretation - vicarious substitution, one suffering in the place of others - is the chapter's most contested freight and is set out in commentary as a hedged reading (Blenkinsopp; Baltzer, Deutero-Isaiah, Hermeneia) rather than asserted by the plain lexemes; nāśāʾ in particular is the ordinary verb for 'bear/carry (guilt, sin)' throughout the priestly and prophetic corpus.

entries.strongs: H6293 (pāḡaʿ 'meet, encounter, strike; Hiphil: cause to meet/strike, interpose, intercede')
entries.lemma: Hiphil of pāḡaʿ, at 53:6 'caused [iniquity] to strike/fall upon him' and at 53:12 'made intercession / interposed for'
entries.partOfSpeech: verb (Hiphil), the framing inclusio of the poem
entries.literal: he made [it] strike/meet upon him … he interposes/intercedes for
entries.standardEnglish: hath laid on him (ASV, 53:6); made intercession (ASV, 53:12)
entries.wohChoice: 53:6 'YHWH has laid upon him the iniquity of us all' (the causative 'cause to fall/strike upon'); 53:12 'made intercession for the transgressors' (the 'interpose/intercede' sense) - the shared root rendered by its two contextual senses, the deliberate inclusio noted in commentary.
entries.rationale: The Hiphil of פָּגַע (H6293; base sense 'meet, encounter, strike') means 'cause to meet, cause to strike/fall upon' and, by extension, 'interpose, make intercession' (BDB, HALOT). At 53:6 YHWH 'caused the iniquity of us all to strike/fall upon' the servant - the standard 'laid on him the iniquity of us all' (ASV/JPS); at 53:12 the same Hiphil is 'made intercession / interposed for the transgressors' (ASV/JPS). Both are the standard versional renderings and carry no lens; the entry is direct. The two occurrences frame the poem's central movement as a deliberate inclusio - the root that made iniquity strike the servant returns to have him interpose for the guilty - a literary feature developed in commentary (Goldingay & Payne, ICC Isaiah 40-55); the alternative causative reading of 53:12 ('cause [judgment] to strike the transgressors') is noted but declined, since the intercession sense fits the servant's vindication.

entries.strongs: H430 (ʾĕlōhîm); H5221 (nāḵāh 'strike, smite')
entries.lemma: ʾĕlōhîm in the phrase mukkēh ʾĕlōhîm 'smitten of God', reporting the onlookers' mistaken judgment
entries.partOfSpeech: divine noun (here in the divine-passive construct 'God-smitten')
entries.literal: struck/smitten of God
entries.standardEnglish: stricken, smitten of God (ASV); struck down by God (NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: 'struck down by God' - ʾĕlōhîm rendered 'God' at the standard surface; the corpus 'the Elohim' convention (central entry elohim-as-translation) is deliberately NOT applied to this line, because the clause reports a misperception the poem then corrects (53:5).
entries.rationale: The corpus elsewhere renders אֱלֹהִים as 'the Elohim' (central entry elohim-as-translation, scoped to Genesis 1), but that convention is deliberately withheld here and אֱלֹהִים is rendered 'God' - the standard value (ASV 'smitten of God'; NRSV 'struck down by God'). The reason is lens-discipline, not lexicon: מֻכֵּה אֱלֹהִים belongs to the clause 'we accounted him stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted', which reports the mistaken judgment of the onlookers - that the servant's suffering marked him as one God had punished - a judgment the very next verse overturns ('but he was pierced because of OUR transgressions', 53:5). To read 'struck down by the Elohim' would import the corpus lens onto the one line the poem stages in order to reject it, an accuracy-before-lens overreach; and because the elohim-as-translation entry's own wohChoice is 'the Elohim', it cannot govern a line whose rendering is 'God', so 53:4 is NOT added to that central entry's appliesTo. Grammatically mukkēh ʾĕlōhîm is best taken as a divine-passive / superlative-of-severity ('God-smitten', a stricken man) reporting appearance, not a claim about agency (Goldingay & Payne, ICC Isaiah 40-55; Blenkinsopp).

entries.strongs: H1504 (gāzar 'cut, divide, cut off')
entries.lemma: niḡzar (Niphal of gzr 'be cut off, severed'), 'cut off from the land of the living' - the servant's death
entries.literal: he was cut off from the land of the living
entries.standardEnglish: he was cut off out of the land of the living (ASV/JPS/NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: 'he was cut off from the land of the living' - niḡzar 'severed/cut off', read as a plain statement of the servant's death (the death that 53:9 then buries).
entries.rationale: נִגְזַר is a Niphal of גזר 'to cut, divide, cut off' (BDB, HALOT); 'cut off from the land of the living' (ʾereṣ ḥayyîm) is the standard idiom for death (cf. Jer 11:19; Ezek 32:23-27), rendered as the versions render it (ASV/JPS/NRSV). The clause states the servant's death plainly - reinforced by the burial of 53:9 (grave, 'in his death') and the 'poured out his life to death' of 53:12 - and the entry is direct with no lens carried. The point is recorded because the reality of the servant's death is load-bearing for the whole interpretive debate (whether the figure is an individual who dies and is vindicated, or a corporate entity), a matter developed in commentary rather than the line (Blenkinsopp; North).

entries.strongs: H4194 (māweṯ 'death'), here plural with 3ms suffix
entries.lemma: bᵉmōṯāyw (formally plural 'in his deaths'), rendered singular 'in his death'; the burial-verse form-crux
entries.partOfSpeech: noun (plural of māweṯ with 3ms suffix; preposition bᵉ-)
entries.literal: in his deaths
entries.standardEnglish: in his death (ASV/JPS/NRSV, reading the plural as singular)
entries.wohChoice: 'in his death' - the formally plural מֹתָיו rendered as a singular (plural of intensity/abstraction); the MT retained against the 1QIsaᵃ variant bāmāṯô 'his burial-mound', which is disclosed.
entries.rationale: בְמֹתָיו is formally the plural of מָוֶת 'death' with a 3ms suffix ('in his deaths'), but is rendered as a singular 'in his death' - a plural of intensity or abstraction, the reading of the versions (ASV/JPS/NRSV) and commentators (Goldingay & Payne, ICC Isaiah 40-55). The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ) reads instead בומתו, widely vocalized bāmāṯô 'his high place / burial-mound', which some prefer for the sense 'tomb' parallel to 'grave' in the first colon; the translation retains the Masoretic consonantal text and discloses the scroll variant for the reader's audit. The rendering is standard and carries no lens; the entry is direct, recording the form-crux together with the burial-context decision (the servant assigned a grave 'with the wicked' and 'with a rich man', the Masoretic 'rich' retained against proposed emendations).

entries.strongs: H817 (ʾāšām 'guilt-offering, reparation-offering'); H5315 (nep̄eš); H7760 (śîm)
entries.lemma: the construction 'if his life (nep̄eš) is set as an ʾāšām (guilt-offering)' - a human life offered as the Levitical reparation-offering (Isa 53:10)
entries.partOfSpeech: conditional clause; the noun ʾāšām is governed cross-corpus by ashem-asham-guilt-bearing-vocabulary
entries.literal: if you/it set(s) his soul (as) a guilt-offering
entries.standardEnglish: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin (ASV); when you make his life a guilt offering (NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: 'if his life is set down as a guilt-offering' - the ʾāšām rendered as the Levitical guilt-/reparation-offering (cross-referencing the central entry ashem-asham-guilt-bearing-vocabulary, whose appliesTo is extended to ISA-53:10 by orchestrator diff), with the uncertain subject of tāśîm left unresolved by an impersonal passive.
entries.rationale: אָשָׁם is the technical Levitical guilt- / reparation-offering (Lev 5:14-6:7; 7:1-7), governed as a cross-corpus lexeme by the central entry ashem-asham-guilt-bearing-vocabulary (whose appliesTo is extended to ISA-53:10 by orchestrator diff); this overlay entry records the text-specific CONSTRUCTION at 53:10, distinct from the bare-lexeme decision. The distinctive and much-debated feature is that a human life (נַפְשׁוֹ 'his nep̄eš/soul/life') is what is 'set' as the ʾāšām, and the subject of תָּשִׂים is grammatically uncertain - 2ms 'if you (YHWH) make his life a guilt-offering' or a 3fs 'if his life is made / makes itself a guilt-offering'; the translation uses an impersonal passive ('if his life is set down as a guilt-offering') and does not resolve the subject, following the range of the versions (ASV/NRSV). The rendering of ʾāšām is standard and carries no lens, so the entry is direct; the application of the cultic reparation-offering to a person - the interpretive core of the verse and the seed of the vicarious-atonement reading - is set out as a hedged reading in commentary (Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 40-55, AB 19A, 2002; Baltzer, Deutero-Isaiah, Hermeneia), not asserted in the line.

entries.strongs: H7200 (rāʾāh 'see'); H7646 (śāḇaʿ 'be satisfied'); H216 (ʾôr 'light')
entries.lemma: the 53:11 text-critical variant - MT 'he shall see, be satisfied' vs the Qumran/Old-Greek 'he shall see light'
entries.partOfSpeech: verb + (MT) verb / (variant) noun object - a text-critical variant
entries.literal: he shall see, [and] be satisfied (MT); he shall see light (DSS/LXX)
entries.standardEnglish: he shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied (ASV, MT); 'he shall see light' (RSV/NRSV/NJPS-margin, following the scrolls/LXX)
entries.wohChoice: retain MT 'he shall see; he shall be satisfied' in the line; disclose the 1QIsaᵃ / 1QIsaᵇ / LXX reading yirʾeh ʾôr 'he shall see light' as a text-critical datum in commentary - the variant materially strengthens the vindication/resurrection reading; 'light' is NOT imported into the MT-based line.
entries.rationale: The Masoretic text reads מֵעֲמַל נַפְשׁוֹ יִרְאֶה יִשְׂבָּע 'out of the toil of his soul he shall see; he shall be satisfied', with no object for 'see'; both Great Isaiah Scrolls (1QIsaᵃ and 1QIsaᵇ) and the Old Greek (LXX 'to show him light') read יִרְאֶה אוֹר 'he shall see light' - an object 'light' (ʾôr) after 'see', an easy near-homograph before the following word. This is a genuine, well-known variant adopted by several modern critical versions (RSV/NRSV/NJPS margin) and discussed at length in the commentaries (Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 40-55, AB 19A, 2002; Goldingay & Payne, ICC Isaiah 40-55). The project translates the Masoretic text and so retains 'he shall see; he shall be satisfied', disclosing the scroll/LXX 'light' reading in commentary for the reader's audit; the variant is materially significant because 'seeing light' after the death of 53:8-9 sharpens the vindication-beyond-death (resurrection) reading, and honest disclosure - rather than silent adoption or suppression - is the accuracy-first handling. The entry is direct: it records a textual fact and imports no lens into the line.

entries.strongs: H776 (ʾereṣ); H1238 (bqq 'empty out'); H1110 (blq 'lay waste'); H5753 (ʿwh 'bend, twist')
entries.lemma: ʾereṣ 'earth/land' in the cosmic-universal register of the Little Apocalypse; with the bqq/blq/bzz emptying-plundering vocabulary of 24:1,3 and ʿiwwāh p̄ānehā 'twists its surface'
entries.partOfSpeech: noun (feminine); the chapter's key term — a rendering-scope decision
entries.literal: the earth / the land
entries.standardEnglish: the earth (ASV 'maketh the earth empty'; JPS) — cosmic scope
entries.wohChoice: 'the earth' — hā-ʾāreṣ rendered in its cosmic-universal scope throughout chapter 24 (the world-judgment register), with the Genesis-1 corpus rendering ʾereṣ='land' (local/durational) deliberately NOT applied; ʿiwwāh p̄ānehā 'twists its surface' (over ASV 'turneth it upside down').
entries.rationale: The Little Apocalypse (Isa 24-27) opens with YHWH bôqēq (bqq 'empty out') and bôlqāh (blq 'lay waste, despoil') hā-ʾāreṣ — an assonant near-synonym pair intensified in 24:3 by the doubled infinitive-absolute hibbôq tibbôq … hibbôz tibbôz (governed by the central harbah-arbeh-doubled-infinitive-intensive entry). The scope of hā-ʾāreṣ is the chapter's governing rendering decision: the Genesis-1-scoped corpus entry renders ʾereṣ 'land' in a local, durational register, and that entry is deliberately withheld here because chs. 24-27 alternate hā-ʾāreṣ with tēḇēl 'the (whole) world' (24:4) and pair it with the universal hā-ʾăḏāmāh 'the ground' and 'the kings of the ground' (24:21) — a world-judgment register read cosmically by ASV, JPS, and the standard commentators (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27, Continental, 1997; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39, AB 19, 2000; Kaiser, Isaiah 13-39, OTL). ʿiwwāh p̄ānehā is rendered 'twists its surface' (ʿwh 'bend, twist' + pānîm 'face/surface'), the concrete image of a distorted face of the ground, rather than ASV's 'turneth it upside down'. The rendering is the standard scholarly one and carries no lens; the entry records the deliberate non-application of the Gen-1 ʾereṣ='land' convention to the cosmic register as the chapter's scope-decision.

entries.source: וְהָאָרֶץ חָנְפָה תַּחַת יֹשְׁבֶיהָ … הֵפֵרוּ בְּרִית עוֹלָם
entries.translit: wᵉhā-ʾāreṣ ḥānᵉp̄āh taḥaṯ yōšᵉḇehā … hēp̄ērû bᵉrîṯ ʿôlām
entries.strongs: H2610 (ḥānēp̄ 'be polluted, profaned'); H8451 (tôrāh); H2706 (ḥōq); H6565 (pārar 'break'); H1285+H5769 (bᵉrîṯ ʿôlām)
entries.lemma: ḥānᵉp̄āh (ḥnp 'be polluted, profaned') + the covenant triad tôrōṯ / ḥōq / bᵉrîṯ-ʿôlām — the earth defiled and the everlasting covenant broken
entries.literal: and the earth is polluted under its inhabitants … they have broken the everlasting covenant
entries.standardEnglish: the earth is defiled/polluted under its inhabitants … broken the everlasting covenant (ASV/JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'the earth lies defiled under its inhabitants … broken the everlasting covenant' — ḥānᵉp̄āh 'defiled/polluted'; bᵉrîṯ ʿôlām 'everlasting covenant' (governed by the central brit-olam entry, appliesTo extended to ISA-24:5); the referent of the covenant deliberately left unidentified.
entries.rationale: ḥnp (H2610) denotes moral pollution/profanation of the land (BDB, HALOT; cf. Num 35:33; Jer 3:1-2), rendered 'lies defiled' — the earth polluted 'under' its inhabitants by the transgressions itemized in the following triad: they 'transgressed the teachings (tôrōṯ), overstepped the statute (ḥōq), broke the everlasting covenant (bᵉrîṯ ʿôlām)'. bᵉrîṯ ʿôlām is the standard 'everlasting covenant', governed by the central brit-olam entry whose own forward-reference already names Isa 24:5 as an extension target (the central appliesTo is extended to ISA-24:5 by orchestrator diff); ʿôlām is durational 'far-distant time', not metaphysical eternity. The referent of the covenant is disputed and is deliberately left unidentified in the line: the Noahic universal ordinance of Gen 9:16 (the same bᵉrîṯ ʿôlām, binding all humanity — the reading most at home in a world-judgment, favored by Wildberger and Blenkinsopp), the Sinai covenant / Torah (paired here with tôrōṯ and ḥōq), or a broader order-of-creation. The universal-Noahic reading is canon-adjacent — a primeval covenant binding all humanity, now avenged on the whole earth — but the Hebrew names no referent, and accuracy-before-lens forbids resolving it in the text; the rendering is standard and the entry is direct.

entries.source: אָלָה אָכְלָה אֶרֶץ … חָרוּ יֹשְׁבֵי אֶרֶץ וְנִשְׁאַר אֱנוֹשׁ מִזְעָר
entries.translit: ʾālāh ʾāḵᵉlāh ʾereṣ … ḥārû yōšᵉḇê ʾereṣ wᵉnišʾar ʾĕnôš mizʿār
entries.strongs: H423 (ʾālāh 'sworn curse, oath'); H398 (ʾākal 'devour'); H2787 (ḥārar 'be scorched, burned'); H582 (ʾĕnôš 'man, mortal')
entries.lemma: ʾālāh 'sworn curse, covenant-imprecation' devouring the earth; with ḥārû (ḥrr 'be scorched') form-crux and ʾĕnôš mizʿār 'few mortals left'
entries.literal: a curse/oath has devoured the earth … the inhabitants of the earth are scorched, and few mortals are left
entries.standardEnglish: a curse hath devoured the earth … the inhabitants are scorched/burned (ASV/JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'a curse has devoured the earth … the inhabitants of the earth are scorched' — ʾālāh as the sworn covenant-curse (not a generic malediction) now falling on the broken bᵉrîṯ of v5; ḥārû 'are scorched' (ḥrr), with the 'dwindle/grow pale' parsing noted.
entries.rationale: ʾālāh (H423) is specifically the sworn imprecation attached to a covenant — the self-maledictory oath invoked when the covenant is broken (BDB, HALOT; cf. Deut 29:19-20; Gen 24:41) — not a generic curse, and it is bound tightly here to the broken bᵉrîṯ ʿôlām of v5 by the opening 'therefore' (ʿal-kēn). The translation keeps 'a curse has devoured the earth' (ASV/JPS), the covenant-oath now consuming the land it once sanctioned; the sworn-oath nuance is the philological point and is standard. ḥārû is a form-crux: the majority derive it from ḥrr 'be scorched, burned' (ASV/JPS 'are scorched/burned', the inhabitants dried like the parched land), while some moderns parse ḥwr/ḥrh 'grow pale, dwindle'; the translation reads 'are scorched' with the minority reading recorded (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Kaiser, Isaiah 13-39, OTL). ʾĕnôš mizʿār 'few mortals are left' uses the collective ʾĕnôš for frail humanity and anticipates the gleaning-remnant image of v13; the renderings are standard and carry no lens.

entries.strongs: H7151 (qiryāh 'city'); H8414 (tōhû)
entries.lemma: qiryaṯ-tōhû 'city of tōhû'; the bare singular tōhû (distinct from the Gen 1:2 tōhû wā-ḇōhû pair)
entries.literal: city of chaos / formlessness / nothingness
entries.standardEnglish: city of confusion (ASV); city of chaos (JPS/NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: 'the city of chaos' — the bare tōhû rendered 'chaos' (the formlessness/nothingness sense, JPS register); the corpus tohu-vavohu entry (which governs the Gen 1:2 PAIR, rendered 'wasteland and emptiness') deliberately NOT applied to the singular construct; the Gen 1:2 / Isa 34:11 tōhû resonance carried in commentary.
entries.rationale: tōhû (H8414) is the same lexeme as the tōhû wā-ḇōhû 'wasteland and emptiness' of Gen 1:2 and the post-judgment tōhû of Isa 34:11 (where it pairs with ḇōhû over a depopulated ruin); here it stands alone in a bound construct qiryaṯ-tōhû 'city of tōhû', naming the chapter's unnamed anti-city, broken and shut up (24:10-12). The central tohu-vavohu entry governs the Genesis alliterative PAIR and renders 'wasteland and emptiness'; that entry is deliberately not applied to the bare singular, and the translation renders 'city of chaos' (JPS/NRSV; ASV 'city of confusion') — the formlessness/nothingness/desolation sense the singular carries — rather than importing the Genesis 'wasteland' rendering onto a different construction (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39). The cross-corpus resonance is genuine and canon-salient — a judged city reduced to the pre-ordered tōhû, an ordering-project reversed into desolation — but it is a matter of the shared lexeme and is carried in commentary, not asserted in the line; the rendering is standard and the entry is direct.

entries.strongs: H217 (ʾûr 'flame, fire, light'); cf. H216 (ʾôr 'light'); H224 (ʾûrîm)
entries.lemma: bā-ʾurîm — a textual crux: 'in the fires' / 'in the east, the regions of light' / (emended) 'in the coastlands'
entries.literal: in the fires / in the lights / in the region(s) of light
entries.standardEnglish: in the east (ASV); in the regions of light (JPS 1917)
entries.wohChoice: 'in the regions of light' (JPS 1917) — MT bā-ʾurîm retained (not emended); the 'in the fires' (ʾûr) reading and the emendation to bā-ʾiyyîm 'in the coastlands' disclosed as alternatives, not adopted.
entries.rationale: bā-ʾurîm is a genuine crux with three live construals: 'in the fires/flames' (ʾûr H217 'fire', a place of ordeal or of the dawn-fires); 'in the east / the regions of light' (the quarter of the rising light, taking ʾûr as a light-region, so JPS 1917 'in the regions of light', ASV 'in the east'); or an emendation to bā-ʾiyyîm 'in the coastlands/isles' to parallel the following bᵉʾiyyê hay-yām 'in the coastlands of the sea'. The direction in which YHWH is to be glorified is at stake, but the consonantal MT reads bʾrym and the translation retains it un-emended, rendering 'in the regions of light' (JPS) with the alternatives disclosed for the reader's audit (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39, discusses the emendation). The decision is text-critical and lexical and carries no lens; the entry records the crux and the MT-retention.

entries.strongs: H430 (ʾĕlōhîm); H3478 (yiśrāʾēl)
entries.lemma: ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl 'the God of Israel' — a construct divine epithet, part of šēm YHWH ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl 'the name of YHWH, the God of Israel'
entries.literal: (the) God of Israel
entries.standardEnglish: the God of Israel (ASV/JPS/NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: 'the God of Israel' — the standard construct epithet; the corpus 'the Elohim' convention (central entry elohim-as-translation, scoped to Genesis 1) deliberately NOT applied to a construct divine epithet in Isaiah, consistent with the Isa 53:4 non-extension.
entries.rationale: The clause names YHWH as šēm YHWH ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl 'the name of YHWH, the God of Israel', a construct epithet in which ʾĕlōhê is the bound form of ʾĕlōhîm. The corpus renders standalone ʾĕlōhîm 'the Elohim' (central entry elohim-as-translation, scoped to Genesis 1), but that convention is deliberately withheld from a construct divine epithet here, exactly as at Isa 53:4 (mukkēh ʾĕlōhîm rendered 'God'): the entry's own wohChoice is 'the Elohim', which cannot govern a bound epithet whose natural English is 'God of Israel', and ISA-24:15 is therefore NOT added to that central entry's appliesTo. The Gen 33:20 el-elohei-yisrael entry transliterates a proper-name altar-designation, a different case; here the standard 'the God of Israel' (ASV/JPS/NRSV) is the accuracy-before-lens rendering. The decision is a lens-discipline record and carries no lens into the text; the entry is direct.

entries.strongs: H7329 (rāzāh 'grow lean'); cf. H7328 (rāz 'secret, mystery'); H6643 (ṣᵉḇî 'beauty, glory'); H6662 (ṣaddîq)
entries.lemma: rāzî-lî (doubled cry): 'leanness/wasting to me' (rzh) vs 'my secret is mine' (rāz); with ṣᵉḇî la-ṣaddîq 'glory to the righteous one'
entries.literal: leanness/wasting is mine, leanness is mine (or: my secret is mine) … beauty/glory to the righteous one
entries.standardEnglish: I pine away, I pine away (ASV); I waste away, I waste away (JPS/NRSV); Glory to the righteous one (ASV/JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'I waste away, I waste away' — from rāzāh 'grow lean' (the leanness/pining sense, ASV/JPS); the rāz 'secret/mystery' reading (Aramaic-type, cf. Dan 2) noted and declined. ṣᵉḇî la-ṣaddîq 'Glory to the righteous one'.
entries.rationale: rāzî-lî is a doubled exclamatory crux. The majority reading derives rāzî from rāzāh 'grow lean, waste away' (H7329; cf. the noun rāzôn 'leanness'), giving 'I waste away / I pine away' (ASV 'I pine away'; JPS/NRSV 'I waste away'), a cry of distress set against the praise just heard 'from the edge of the earth'. A minority take rāz 'secret, mystery' (H7328, an Aramaic-type loan attested at Dan 2:18-19 etc.), giving 'my secret is mine' — a reading with obvious appeal but weak support in this text, and it is noted and declined here (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Kaiser, Isaiah 13-39). The preceding colon ṣᵉḇî la-ṣaddîq is rendered 'Glory to the righteous one' (ṣᵉḇî 'beauty, splendor, glory'; ASV/JPS), and the verse closes on the fivefold bgd treachery-paronomasia (bōḡᵉḏîm bāḡāḏû ûḇeḡeḏ bôḡᵉḏîm bāḡāḏû), rendered by repetition rather than reproduced as sound; the chosen renderings are standard and carry no lens, and the entry records the rzh/rāz crux.

entries.strongs: H699 (ʾărubbāh 'window, sluice, floodgate'); H4791 (mārôm 'height, on high'); H6605 (pāṯaḥ 'open'); H4146 (môsāḏ 'foundation'); H7493 (rāʿaš 'quake')
entries.lemma: ʾărubbôṯ mimmārôm 'the windows from on high' (the Flood-echo lattice-openings, H699 as at Gen 7:11) + môsᵉḏê ʾāreṣ 'foundations of the earth' quaking
entries.partOfSpeech: noun (construct plural) + prepositional phrase — the Flood-reversal image
entries.literal: windows/sluices from on high are opened … the foundations of the earth quake
entries.standardEnglish: the windows on high are opened … the foundations of the earth tremble (ASV/JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'the windows on high are opened, and the foundations of the earth quake' — ʾărubbôṯ rendered plainly 'windows on high' (NOT the Genesis lens-tilted 'floodgates'); the deliberate Flood echo of Gen 7:11 carried in commentary; the central arubot-ha-shamayim entry deliberately NOT extended here.
entries.rationale: ʾărubbāh (H699) is the lattice-opening, sluice, or floodgate — the same lexeme as the ʾărubbōṯ haš-šāmayim 'windows of the skies' of the Genesis Flood (Gen 7:11); the opening of the windows above (mimmārôm 'from on high') together with the shaking of the môsᵉḏê ʾāreṣ 'foundations of the earth' below is a deliberate Flood-reversal echo — the sealed cosmos unsealed from above and below, the escape-is-impossible terror/pit/snare tricolon of vv17-18 building to this cosmic cause (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39). The translation renders the plain 'windows on high' (ASV/JPS) and does NOT import the central arubot-ha-shamayim entry's lens-tilted 'floodgates of the skies': the construct differs (mimmārôm 'from on high', not haš-šāmayim 'of the skies'), the rendering differs, and per the accuracy-before-lens rule an entry whose wohChoice is 'floodgates of the skies' cannot govern a line rendered 'windows on high' — so ISA-24:18 is deliberately NOT added to that central entry's appliesTo (the same non-extension logic as elohim-as-translation @ ISA-53:4). The Flood link is genuine and canon-adjacent — the primeval world-drowning re-invoked as the pattern of the coming world-judgment — but it is documented in this overlay entry and in commentary, not surfaced in the text; the entry is direct.

entries.source: צְבָא הַמָּרוֹם בַּמָּרוֹם … וְעַל־מַלְכֵי הָאֲדָמָה עַל־הָאֲדָמָה
entries.translit: ṣᵉḇāʾ ham-mārôm bam-mārôm … wᵉʿal-malḵê hā-ʾăḏāmāh ʿal-hā-ʾăḏāmāh
entries.strongs: H6635 (ṣāḇāʾ 'host, army'); H4791 (mārôm 'height, high place'); H6485 (pāqad 'visit, punish'); H127 (ʾăḏāmāh 'ground'); H4428 (meleḵ 'king')
entries.lemma: ṣᵉḇāʾ ham-mārôm 'the host of the height/heaven on high' — a heavenly host JUDGED by YHWH (distinct from the divine title YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ, v23); with the mārôm↔ʾăḏāmāh height/ground antithesis
entries.literal: the host of the height, in the height
entries.standardEnglish: the host of the high ones (ASV); the host of the high heaven (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'the host of the height on high' — the plain rendering (ASV/JPS register), committing to NO identification; the rebellious-heavenly-host / divine-council, astral-host, and angelic-patron-princes readings are set out as hedged, apparatus-only options in commentary. Grammatically and referentially DISTINCT from YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ (v23, the divine title).
entries.rationale: At 24:21 YHWH yip̄qōḏ 'brings punishment upon' ṣᵉḇāʾ ham-mārôm bam-mārôm 'the host of the height on high' and, in parallel, malḵê hā-ʾăḏāmāh ʿal-hā-ʾăḏāmāh 'the kings of the ground upon the ground' — a pointed mārôm↔ʾăḏāmāh (height↔ground) antithesis pairing a heavenly object of judgment with an earthly one. The plain 'the host of the height on high' (ASV 'the host of the high ones'; JPS 'the host of the high heaven') is the direct rendering, and the translation commits to no identification: this ṣᵉḇāʾ is a host that YHWH PUNISHES and is grammatically and referentially DISTINCT from the divine title YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ 'YHWH of hosts' of v23, where YHWH commands the hosts (overlay yhwh-tzevaot-hosts-isaiah). Beyond the line the referent is open and lens-salient, and these readings are hedged and apparatus-only: (a) rebellious/disloyal heavenly beings, members of the divine council judged by their head (E. T. Mullen, The Divine Council in Canaanite and Early Hebrew Literature, HSM 24, 1980; F. M. Cross, Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic, 1973); (b) the astral host — sun, moon, and stars worshipped as powers, chiming with the disgraced luminaries of v23; (c) the angelic patron-princes of the nations set over the earthly kings (cf. Deut 32:8 LXX; Dan 10). The later Second-Temple tradition read a heavenly host bound and imprisoned (1 Enoch 18:13-16; 21:1-10; the central fallen-stars-prison-1-enoch-18-21 entry), and v22 continues with exactly that imprisonment; but the rebellious-host identification is INFERRED and is deliberately confined to the apparatus — accuracy-before-lens forbids imposing it on the text, and the central fallen-stars-prison entry is NOT extended to ISA-24:21/22. The entry is therefore direct: the wohChoice and the line commit only to the plain 'host of the height on high'.

entries.source: וְאֻסְּפוּ אֲסֵפָה אַסִּיר עַל־בּוֹר וְסֻגְּרוּ עַל־מַסְגֵּר וּמֵרֹב יָמִים יִפָּקֵדוּ
entries.translit: wᵉʾussᵉp̄û ʾăsēp̄āh ʾassîr ʿal-bôr wᵉsuggᵉrû ʿal-masgēr ûmērōḇ yāmîm yippāqēḏû
entries.strongs: H6485 (pāqad 'visit, muster, appoint, punish'); H953 (bôr 'pit, cistern'); H4525 (masgēr 'dungeon, prison'); H616 (ʾassîr 'prisoner'); H622 (ʾāsap̄ 'gather')
entries.lemma: yippāqēḏû (Niphal of pqd) 'be punished / be visited/mustered' — closing the paqad inclusio with yip̄qōḏ (v21); with bôr 'pit-prison' (Sheol resonance) and masgēr 'dungeon'
entries.literal: they shall be gathered … as a prisoner into a pit … shut up in a dungeon … and after many days they shall be visited/punished
entries.standardEnglish: gathered … as prisoners are gathered in the pit … after many days shall they be visited/punished (ASV/JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'they shall be punished' — pqd rendered 'punished' (ASV/JPS, the judgment continued), with the neutral 'be visited / mustered / attended to' (possibly for release) flagged as a live ambiguity; bôr 'pit' as the prison-cistern with an underworld/Sheol resonance; masgēr 'dungeon'.
entries.rationale: yippāqēḏû is a Niphal of pqd (H6485), the same root as yip̄qōḏ 'will punish/visit' in v21, closing a deliberate paqad inclusio over the two-verse unit; the root's wide semantic range ('visit, muster, attend to, appoint, punish') makes the form genuinely ambiguous — 'they shall be punished' (ASV/JPS, continuing the judgment) or, neutrally, 'they shall be visited / mustered / attended to', leaving open whether for punishment or for eventual release after the 'many days' (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39, notes the openness). The translation reads 'they shall be punished' with the visitation-ambiguity flagged, the standard versional choice. bôr (H953) is the pit/cistern used as a prison (cf. Gen 37:24; Jer 38:6) and carries an underworld/Sheol resonance; masgēr (H4525) is the dungeon/lock-up; the gathering of the judged 'as prisoners into a pit', 'shut up', and 'visited after many days' is the imprisonment-of-cosmic-rebels image the later tradition develops at 1 Enoch 18-21 (the central fallen-stars-prison-1-enoch-18-21 entry, referenced in commentary, not applied). The renderings are standard and carry no lens; the entry records the pqd inclusio and the punish/visit ambiguity.

entries.source: וְחָפְרָה הַלְּבָנָה וּבוֹשָׁה הַחַמָּה … וְנֶגֶד זְקֵנָיו כָּבוֹד
entries.translit: wᵉḥāp̄ᵉrāh hal-lᵉḇānāh ûḇôšāh haḥ-ḥammāh … wᵉneḡeḏ zᵉqēnāyw kāḇôḏ
entries.strongs: H3842 (lᵉḇānāh 'moon'); H2535 (ḥammāh 'sun, heat'); H2659 (ḥāp̄ēr 'be abashed, ashamed'); H954 (bôš 'be ashamed'); H3519 (kāḇôḏ 'glory'); H2205 (zāqēn 'elder')
entries.lemma: the bare absolute kāḇôḏ 'glory' (distinct from the construct kᵉḇôḏ-YHWH and the suffixed kᵉḇôḏô); with lᵉḇānāh 'the white one' / ḥammāh 'the hot one' (moon/sun) and zᵉqēnāyw 'his elders'
entries.partOfSpeech: noun (absolute, predicate of a verbless clause) + poetic luminary-names
entries.literal: the moon shall be abashed and the sun ashamed … and before his elders (is) glory
entries.standardEnglish: the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed … before his elders shall be glory (ASV/JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'the moon shall be abashed and the sun ashamed … before his elders is glory' — lᵉḇānāh/ḥammāh rendered plainly 'moon'/'sun'; the bare absolute kāḇôḏ 'glory' at the standard surface, the weighty radiant physical-presence register (the kāḇôḏ-tradition of Isa 6:3, Ezek 1:28) carried in commentary. Governed by neither the Ezekiel construct nor the Isa-6:3 suffixed kavod entry.
entries.rationale: The chapter closes with the moon abashed (ḥpr II 'be ashamed, abashed', H2659) and the sun ashamed (bwš, H954), named poetically lᵉḇānāh 'the white one' (H3842) and ḥammāh 'the hot one' (H2535); the translation renders them plainly 'moon' and 'sun' (ASV/JPS). This is not the darkening-portent of the Day-of-YHWH tradition (Joel 2:10; cf. the central cosmic-signs cluster) but the luminaries outshone and put to shame because YHWH's own radiance eclipses them — the kî-clause 'for YHWH of hosts reigns' supplies the reason, and Isa 60:19-20 develops the same image (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39). The closing wᵉneḡeḏ zᵉqēnāyw kāḇôḏ 'and before his elders is glory' ends on a bare, absolute kāḇôḏ — neither the construct kᵉḇôḏ-YHWH of the Ezekiel-scoped kavod-yhwh entry nor the suffixed kᵉḇôḏô of the Isa-6:3 kevodo-kavod-suffixed entry, and so governed by neither; the translation keeps the standard 'glory'. The weighty, radiant physical-presence register of kāḇôḏ (the kāḇôḏ-tradition of Isa 6:3 and Ezek 1:28) — glory manifest 'before his elders', an enthroned theophany with its attendant assembly (zᵉqēnîm; cf. the elders before the enthroned deity at Ex 24:9-11) — is the canon-salient point and is carried in commentary, not surfaced by re-rendering; the entry is direct.

entries.source: עָשִׂיתָ פֶּלֶא עֵצוֹת מֵרָחוֹק אֱמוּנָה אֹמֶן
entries.translit: ʿāśîṯā peleʾ ʿēṣôṯ mē-rāḥôq ʾĕmûnāh ʾōmen
entries.strongs: H6382 (peleʾ 'wonder'), root H6381 (pālāʾ); H6098 (ʿēṣāh 'counsel, plan'); H7350 (rāḥôq 'far, distant'); H530 (ʾĕmûnāh); H544 (ʾōmen); root H539 (ʾāman 'be firm, reliable')
entries.lemma: the opening-hymn praise vocabulary of 25:1: peleʾ 'wonder', ʿēṣôṯ mē-rāḥôq 'plans from long ago', and the intensified pair ʾĕmûnāh ʾōmen 'sure faithfulness'
entries.literal: you have done a wonder; counsels/plans from afar; faithfulness, sureness
entries.standardEnglish: thou hast done wonderful things; even counsels of old, in faithfulness and truth (ASV); counsels of old, in faithfulness and truth (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'you have done a wonder - plans formed long ago, in faithfulness and truth' - peleʾ 'wonder' (the extraordinary deed); ʿēṣôṯ mē-rāḥôq 'plans formed long ago' (ʿēṣāh 'counsel/plan' + mē-rāḥôq read temporally, 'from of old'); ʾĕmûnāh ʾōmen rendered 'faithfulness and truth' (ASV/JPS), the two ʾmn-nouns treated as an intensified single notion ('sure/steadfast faithfulness') in commentary.
entries.rationale: The verse opens the chapter's thanksgiving hymn with three praise-terms. peleʾ (H6382, from pālāʾ 'be extraordinary') is the wonder/marvel done by YHWH, rendered 'wonder' (ASV 'wonderful things'). ʿēṣôṯ mē-rāḥôq is 'counsels/plans (ʿēṣāh) from afar (mē-rāḥôq)', where rāḥôq is read temporally 'from of old / long ago' (JPS 'counsels of old') - a purpose settled in advance and now executed. ʾĕmûnāh ʾōmen is a figura-etymologica pair from the root ʾmn 'be firm, reliable'; ASV/JPS render 'faithfulness and truth', which the translation keeps while noting in commentary that the doubling is an intensified single notion ('sure/steadfast faithfulness', a hendiadys) rather than two distinct attributes (BDB, HALOT; Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27, Continental, 1997). The 'plans formed long ago' clause - a pre-settled purpose carried out in time - is canon-adjacent, but the rendering is the standard scholarly one and any such resonance is confined to commentary; the entry is direct.

entries.source: יְהוָה אֱלֹהַי אַתָּה … הִנֵּה אֱלֹהֵינוּ זֶה
entries.translit: YHWH ʾĕlōhay ʾattāh … hinnēh ʾĕlōhênû zeh
entries.strongs: H430 (ʾĕlōhîm)
entries.lemma: the suffixed ʾĕlōhîm of the doxology - ʾĕlōhay 'my God' (25:1) and ʾĕlōhênû 'our God' (25:9) - rendered 'my God'/'our God', NOT 'the Elohim'
entries.partOfSpeech: divine noun (suffixed 1cs / 1cp) in first-person praise / acclamation
entries.literal: my God … our God
entries.standardEnglish: my God … our God (ASV/JPS/NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: 'my God' (25:1) / 'our God' (25:9) - the suffixed ʾĕlōhîm rendered plainly; the corpus 'the Elohim' convention (central entry elohim-as-translation, scoped to Genesis 1) deliberately NOT applied to first-person doxology, consistent with the Isa 53:4 (mukkēh ʾĕlōhîm 'God') and 24:15 (ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl 'the God of Israel') non-extensions.
entries.rationale: At 25:1 the hymn addresses YHWH ʾĕlōhay ʾattāh 'YHWH, you are my God' (1cs suffix), and at 25:9 the answering confession cries hinnēh ʾĕlōhênû zeh 'Behold, this is our God' (1cp suffix). The corpus renders standalone ʾĕlōhîm 'the Elohim' (central entry elohim-as-translation), but that convention is scoped to the Genesis-1 narrative frame and is deliberately withheld from a vocative hymn and a confessional acclamation: the entry's own wohChoice 'the Elohim (with article in narrative)' cannot govern a first-person 'my God'/'our God', and ISA-25:1/25:9 are therefore NOT added to that central entry's appliesTo - the same lens-discipline non-extension applied at Isa 53:4 and 24:15. The rendering is the standard versional value (ASV/JPS), accuracy-before-lens, and carries no lens; the entry records the deliberate non-application (Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39, AB 19, 2000).

entries.strongs: H2158 (zāmîr 'song'); cf. H2168 (zāmar 'to prune') and H2156 (zᵉmôrāh 'branch'); H6030 (ʿānāh 'answer') / H6031 (ʿānāh II 'be bowed down, afflicted'); H2114 (zûr, part. zārîm 'strangers'); H6184 (ʿārîṣ 'ruthless, tyrant')
entries.lemma: zᵉmîr ʿārîṣîm yaʿăneh - a double crux (zᵉmîr 'song'/'pruning'; yaʿăneh 'brought low'/'answered'); with zārîm 'strangers'
entries.literal: the song/pruning of the ruthless is brought-low/answered
entries.standardEnglish: the song of the terrible ones shall be brought low (ASV); the song of the tyrants is silenced (NJPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'the song of the ruthless is brought low' - zᵉmîr 'song' (√zmr I), yaʿăneh 'is brought low / humbled' (√ʿnh II); the 'branch/pruning' (√zmr II) and 'is answered/silenced' (√ʿnh I) readings recorded as alternatives. zārîm 'strangers/foreigners' (also 25:2).
entries.rationale: zᵉmîr is ambiguous between √zmr I 'sing' (giving 'song, singing') and √zmr II 'prune' (giving 'pruning, a lopped shoot'), and yaʿăneh between √ʿnh II 'be bowed down, humbled' (giving 'is brought low') and √ʿnh I 'answer, respond' (giving 'is answered / silenced') (BDB, HALOT). The translation follows the majority reading 'the song of the ruthless is brought low' (ASV/JPS) - the exultant song of the tyrants subdued, as the heat is subdued by a cloud's shadow in the same verse's simile - with the botanical 'branch/pruning' image and the 'answered/cut-short' reading recorded as live alternatives (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Kaiser, Isaiah 13-39, OTL, 1974). zārîm 'strangers, foreigners' (√zwr), recurring from 25:2, is rendered 'strangers'; the renderings are standard and carry no lens, and the entry records the double crux.

entries.source: מִשְׁתֵּה שְׁמָנִים מִשְׁתֵּה שְׁמָרִים שְׁמָנִים מְמֻחָיִם שְׁמָרִים מְזֻקָּקִים
entries.translit: mišteh šᵉmānîm mišteh šᵉmārîm šᵉmānîm mᵉmuḥāyim šᵉmārîm mᵉzuqqāqîm
entries.strongs: H4960 (mišteh 'feast, banquet'); H8081 (šemen 'fat, oil', pl. šᵉmānîm); H8105 (šemer, pl. šᵉmārîm 'lees, dregs of wine'); H4221 (mōaḥ 'marrow'; denom. mᵉmuḥāyim 'full of marrow'); H2212 (zāqaq 'refine, strain'; mᵉzuqqāqîm)
entries.lemma: the mountain-banquet menu: mišteh 'feast', šᵉmānîm 'fat/rich foods', šᵉmārîm 'wine on the lees' (mᵉmuḥāyim 'full of marrow', mᵉzuqqāqîm 'well refined')
entries.literal: a feast of fat things, a feast of lees(-wines); fat things full of marrow, lees(-wines) well refined
entries.standardEnglish: a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees (ASV/JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees - of fat things full of marrow, of wines on the lees well refined' - the lavish, inclusive banquet YHWH makes 'for all the peoples' on 'this mountain' (Zion); the eschatological-banquet reading and its NT messianic-banquet reception (Matt 8:11; Luke 14:15-24; Rev 19:9) confined to commentary, not committed in the line.
entries.rationale: mišteh (√šth 'drink') is a feast/banquet, here doubled: šᵉmānîm 'fat/rich things' (šemen 'fat, oil') and šᵉmārîm 'wines on the lees' (šemer 'dregs' - wine long matured on its sediment, hence mature and full-bodied), further qualified as mᵉmuḥāyim 'full of marrow' (denominative of mōaḥ) and mᵉzuqqāqîm 'well refined/strained' (zqq). The banquet is rendered by its standard values (ASV/JPS); the philological point is the deliberately superlative menu of a royal feast. The canon-salient feature - that the feast is spread 'for all the peoples' (lᵉ-ḵol-hā-ʿammîm) on 'this mountain', an inclusive eschatological banquet on Zion - is developed as a hedged reading in commentary (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39; Kaiser, Isaiah 13-39, OTL), together with the messianic-banquet reception the image feeds in the New Testament (the feast with Abraham of Matt 8:11, the great-banquet parable of Luke 14:15-24, the marriage-supper of Rev 19:9); the rendering carries no lens and the entry is direct.

entries.source: וּבִלַּע … פְּנֵי־הַלּוֹט הַלּוֹט עַל־כָּל־הָעַמִּים וְהַמַּסֵּכָה הַנְּסוּכָה
entries.translit: û-ḇillaʿ … pᵉnê-hal-lôṭ hal-lôṭ ʿal-kol-hā-ʿammîm wᵉha-massēḵāh han-nᵉsûḵāh
entries.strongs: H1104 (bālaʿ 'swallow up, engulf, destroy'); H3875 (lôṭ 'covering, veil'), root H3874 (lûṭ 'wrap, envelop'); H4541 (massēḵāh 'woven covering; molten image'); H5258 (nāsaḵ 'pour out') / nsk 'weave' (nᵉsûḵāh)
entries.lemma: the covering-pair of 25:7: hal-lôṭ (doubled) 'the shroud/covering' and ha-massēḵāh han-nᵉsûḵāh 'the veil spread/woven'; billaʿ 'swallow up = destroy'
entries.literal: he will swallow up … the face of the wrapping, the wrapping over all the peoples, and the woven/spread veil
entries.standardEnglish: he will destroy … the face of the covering that covereth all peoples, and the veil that is spread over all nations (ASV/JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'he will swallow up … the face of the shroud that shrouds all the peoples, and the veil that is spread over all the nations' - billaʿ 'swallow up' here in the destroy/do-away-with sense (the same verb that opens 25:8, of Death); hal-lôṭ 'shroud/covering' (√lwṭ 'wrap'), ha-massēḵāh 'veil'; the funerary-shroud reading (tying 25:7 to the death-swallowing of 25:8) noted as context-favoured, and the epistemic-veil (blindness) reading recorded as an alternative.
entries.rationale: billaʿ (√blʿ 'swallow, engulf') is used here in its extended sense 'destroy, do away with' - YHWH removes the covering - and is the deliberate catchword linking this verse to billaʿ ham-māweṯ 'he swallowed up death' in 25:8. hal-lôṭ (doubled hal-lôṭ hal-lôṭ with paseq, from lwṭ 'to wrap, envelop', cf. 1 Sam 21:10) is 'the covering/shroud', and its parallel ha-massēḵāh han-nᵉsûḵāh 'the veil that is spread/woven over all the nations' (nsk 'weave' or 'pour out') confirms the image of an enveloping cover. The translation keeps the standard 'shroud … veil' (ASV/JPS), with the funerary reading - the covering as a death-shroud over the nations, which the death-swallowing of 25:8 then abolishes - noted as the reading the context favours, and the epistemic/mourning-veil (a blinding covering removed) recorded as an alternative (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39); the renderings are standard and carry no lens.
