entries.translit: billaʿ ham-māweṯ lā-neṣaḥ … û-māḥāh … dimʿāh mē-ʿal kol-pānîm
entries.strongs: H1104 (bālaʿ 'swallow up'); H4194 (māweṯ 'death'); H5331 (neṣaḥ 'perpetuity, endurance; [later] victory'); H4229 (māḥāh 'wipe away'); H1832 (dimʿāh 'tears')
entries.lemma: billaʿ ham-māweṯ lā-neṣaḥ 'he has swallowed up death forever' - the death-defeat line; māweṯ rendered abstract 'death' (not personified 'Death'); the neṣaḥ 'forever'/'victory' variant
entries.literal: he has swallowed up death for perpetuity … and he will wipe away tears from upon every face
entries.standardEnglish: He hath swallowed up death for ever (ASV); He will swallow up / destroy death for ever (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'He has swallowed up death forever' - subject YHWH, billaʿ 'swallow up' (from 25:7), ham-māweṯ 'death' rendered abstract (lower-case), NOT personified 'Death'; lā-neṣaḥ 'forever' (MT). The Ugaritic Môtu-reversal (Death the Swallower himself swallowed) and the NT reception / versional variant (LXX inversion; 1 Cor 15:54 neṣaḥ='victory'; Rev 21:4 tear-wiping) are hedged, apparatus-only resonances; the central mot-mavet-death-personified entry's appliesTo is extended to ISA-25:8 to record the cross-corpus governance, the Hebrew/Ugaritic distinction kept in the apparatus (māweṯ rendered 'death', not 'Môtu').
entries.rationale: billaʿ ham-māweṯ lā-neṣaḥ 'he has swallowed up death forever' is the chapter's load-bearing line: the verb blʿ 'swallow up' (from 25:7) is now turned on death itself, with YHWH the implied subject and ham-māweṯ the object; the wiping of tears (û-māḥāh … dimʿāh) follows. The translation renders māweṯ as the abstract 'death' (lower-case) and lā-neṣaḥ 'forever' (neṣaḥ 'perpetuity, endurance', the standard MT sense) - the reading of ASV and JPS, accuracy-before-lens; personified 'Death' is NOT written into the line. Two resonances are disclosed in commentary and kept hedged. (i) The Ugaritic Môtu reversal: Hebrew māweṯ shares the proto-Semitic root √mwt with Ugaritic mt (vocalized Môtu), the Death-god of the Baal Cycle whose iconography is a vast throat that swallows gods and who in KTU 1.5 swallows Baʿlu himself, so the verb blʿ 'swallow' deployed against Death inverts the death-god's standing image (J. Day, God's Conflict with the Dragon and the Sea, 1985). The central entry mot-mavet-death-personified-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible already names Isa 25:8 in its rationale as a Hebrew attestation of this personified-Death tradition, and its wohChoice already provides that the Ugaritic/Hebrew distinction is kept in the apparatus (Ugaritic vocalization only where the source-text is Ugaritic); ISA-25:8 is added to that entry's appliesTo (orchestrator CENTRAL diff) to make the cross-corpus governance auditable, WITHOUT changing the Hebrew line's 'death'. (ii) Reception and the neṣaḥ variant: the Old Greek inverts the clause (katépien ho thánatos ischýsas 'Death, having prevailed, swallowed up', Death as subject), while 1 Cor 15:54 cites the verse in the MT's direction but reads neṣaḥ as 'victory' (katepóthē ho thánatos eis nîkos 'Death is swallowed up in victory', the later-Hebrew/Aramaic sense of nṣḥ); Rev 21:4 echoes the very next clause ('he will wipe away every tear … death shall be no more'). These are versional and reception data, disclosed for audit and not read back into the MT line (Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39, AB 19, 2000). The rendering is the standard MT reading and carries no lens; the entry is direct, with the cross-corpus and reception resonances hedged and apparatus-only.

entries.strongs: H136 (ʾăḏōnāy); H3069 (YHWH pointed with the vowels of ʾĕlōhîm in the compound)
entries.lemma: the compound divine name ʾăḏōnāy YHWH (ʾăḏōnāy + the Tetragrammaton with ʾĕlōhîm-vowels), distinct from the standalone ʾăḏōnāy of Isa 6
entries.literal: my Lord YHWH
entries.standardEnglish: the Lord GOD (JPS/NRSV); the Lord Jehovah (ASV)
entries.wohChoice: 'the Lord YHWH' - the compound name rendered by the corpus compound-name convention (central adonai-yhwh [Ezekiel] and adonai-yhwh-divine-name [Genesis], wohChoice 'Lord YHWH'), keeping the Isaiah YHWH house-style visible; kept distinct from the standalone ʾăḏōnāy 'the Lord' of the Isa 6 overlay entry (adonai-standalone-title-isaiah).
entries.rationale: At 25:8 the compound ʾăḏōnāy YHWH ('my Lord' + the Tetragrammaton, here pointed with the vowels of ʾĕlōhîm - the qere-perpetuum that avoids a double 'Adonai') is the subject of û-māḥāh 'will wipe away'. This is the compound divine name, not the standalone ʾăḏōnāy covered by the Isaiah overlay entry adonai-standalone-title-isaiah (scoped to Isa 6:1/6:8/6:11); the central compound entries adonai-yhwh (Ezekiel) and adonai-yhwh-divine-name (Genesis) render 'Lord YHWH' but are book-scoped and do not list Isaiah, so the compound was lexically uncovered in Isaiah. The Editor renders 'the Lord YHWH' - matching the corpus compound-name convention and keeping the book's YHWH house-style visible for the Tetragrammaton - rather than the reference-PD 'the Lord GOD' (JPS) / 'the Lord Jehovah' (ASV); the two designations (standalone 'the Lord', compound 'the Lord YHWH') are kept distinct so the reader can see the source's own alternation. This is a house-style / divine-name decision consistent across the corpus and carries no lens; the entry is direct.

entries.source: וְנָדוֹשׁ מוֹאָב תַּחְתָּיו כְּהִדּוּשׁ מַתְבֵּן במי [בְּמוֹ] מַדְמֵנָה
entries.translit: wᵉnāḏôš môʾāḇ taḥtāyw kᵉhiddûš maṯbēn bᵉmê(ketiv) / bᵉmô(qere) maḏmēnāh
entries.strongs: H1758 (dûš 'thresh, tread'); H4963 (maṯbēn 'straw-heap'); H4087 (madmēnāh 'dung-heap'), root H1828 (dōmen 'dung'); H3068 (YHWH); H3027 (yāḏ 'hand')
entries.lemma: the Moab-threshing simile with the ketiv/qere bᵉmê/bᵉmô and madmēnāh 'dung-pit'; yaḏ-YHWH 'the hand of YHWH'
entries.literal: Moab shall be trodden down in its place as straw is trodden down in [the water of / within] a dung-heap
entries.standardEnglish: Moab shall be trodden down in his place, even as straw is trodden down in the water of the dunghill (ASV, ketiv); as straw is trodden down in the dunghill (JPS, qere)
entries.wohChoice: 'Moab will be trodden down in its place, as straw is trodden down in a dung-pit' - the qere בְּמוֹ bᵉmô 'in/within' translated (with madmēnāh 'dung-pit/dunghill', √dmn 'dung'), per the qere-first rule; the ketiv במי bᵉmê 'in the water(s) of' (liquid-manure image, so ASV) flagged. yaḏ-YHWH 'the hand of YHWH' rendered plainly (the central yad-yhwh entry is Ezekiel-scoped and NOT applied). The possible paronomasia on the Moabite place-name Madmēn (Jer 48:2) noted.
entries.rationale: The verse threshes Moab like straw: nāḏôš (√dwš 'thresh, tread') 'trodden down' … kᵉhiddûš maṯbēn 'as straw is threshed'. The source carries a ketiv/qere at the final phrase: the consonantal ketiv reads במי bᵉmê 'in the water(s) of', the Masoretic reading-tradition qere reads בְּמוֹ bᵉmô 'in / within'; per the project's qere-first rule the line translates the qere ('in a dung-pit'), with the ketiv ('in the water of a dunghill' - straw trodden into liquid manure, so ASV) recorded for audit. madmēnāh (√dmn 'dung', cf. dōmen 'dung, manure') is the dung-heap/manure-pile (BDB, HALOT); it may also pun on the Moabite toponym Madmēn 'destroyed' of Jer 48:2, a paronomastic echo noted by the commentators (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39). yaḏ-YHWH 'the hand of YHWH' (25:10a, the hand that rests on the mountain) is rendered plainly; the central yad-yhwh entry is scoped to Ezekiel and is deliberately not applied, as in chapter 24. The renderings are standard and carry no lens; the entry records the ketiv/qere, the dung-imagery, and the toponym-paronomasia.

entries.source: כַּאֲשֶׁר יְפָרֵשׂ הַשֹּׂחֶה לִשְׂחוֹת וְהִשְׁפִּיל גַּאֲוָתוֹ עִם אָרְבּוֹת יָדָיו
entries.translit: kaʾăšer yᵉp̄ārēś haś-śōḥeh li-śḥôṯ wᵉhišpîl gaʾăwāṯô ʿim ʾārᵉbôṯ yāḏāyw
entries.strongs: H6566 (pāraś 'spread out'); H7811 (śāḥāh 'swim', part. śōḥeh 'swimmer'); H8213 (šāp̄al 'be low', Hiphil 'bring low'); H1346 (gaʾăwāh 'pride'); H693 (ʾārab 'lie in wait, be crafty', ʾārᵉbôṯ 'craft, cunning')
entries.lemma: the swimmer-image close of 25:11: haś-śōḥeh 'the swimmer'; wᵉhišpîl 'he will bring low' (subject YHWH); ʾārᵉbôṯ yāḏāyw 'the cunning of his hands' (crux)
entries.literal: as the swimmer spreads to swim … and he will bring low his pride with the craftiness of his hands
entries.standardEnglish: as he that swimmeth spreadeth forth his hands to swim … he will lay low his pride together with the craft of his hands (ASV); the pride … shall be brought down (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'as a swimmer spreads out his hands to swim; but he will bring down his pride together with the cunning of his hands' - haś-śōḥeh 'the swimmer' (√śḥh); wᵉhišpîl read actively with YHWH as subject (carried over from 25:10), against JPS's passive 'his pride shall be brought down'; ʾārᵉbôṯ yāḏāyw 'the cunning of his hands' (√ʾrb 'lie in wait, be crafty', ASV/JPS), with 'the strokes/spreadings of his hands' (the swimmer's motions) recorded as an alternative.
entries.rationale: Moab flails in the manure-pit like a swimmer: û-p̄ēraś yāḏāyw … kaʾăšer yᵉp̄ārēś haś-śōḥeh li-śḥôṯ 'he will spread out his hands … as a swimmer spreads to swim' (śḥh 'swim'). Two decisions follow. (i) The subject of wᵉhišpîl 'he will bring low' (Hiphil of šp̄l): the translation reads it actively with YHWH as subject (continued from yaḏ-YHWH in 25:10), where JPS leaves the agent implicit with a passive 'his pride shall be brought down'; both are defensible and the active is kept. (ii) ʾārᵉbôṯ yāḏāyw is a crux - from ʾrb 'lie in wait, be crafty', giving 'the cunning/craft of his hands' (ASV/JPS), against a derivation giving 'the outspreadings/strokes of his hands' (the swimmer's flailing motions), and a minority 'the joints/limbs'; the translation follows 'the cunning of his hands' (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Kaiser, Isaiah 13-39, OTL). The renderings are standard and carry no lens; the entry records the swimmer-image, the subject-ambiguity, and the ʾārᵉbôṯ crux.

entries.source: וּמִבְצַר מִשְׂגַּב חוֹמֹתֶיךָ הֵשַׁח הִשְׁפִּיל הִגִּיעַ לָאָרֶץ עַד־עָפָר
entries.translit: û-miḇṣar miśgaḇ ḥômōṯeḵā hēšaḥ hišpîl higgîaʿ lā-ʾāreṣ ʿaḏ-ʿāp̄ār
entries.strongs: H4013 (miḇṣār 'fortress'); H4869 (miśgāḇ 'high refuge, secure height'); H2346 (ḥômāh 'wall'); H7817 (šāḥaḥ 'bow down', Hiphil hēšaḥ); H8213 (šāp̄al, Hiphil hišpîl); H5060 (nāḡaʿ, Hiphil higgîaʿ 'reach, bring'); H6083 (ʿāp̄ār 'dust')
entries.lemma: the fortress-demolition triplet of 25:12: miḇṣar miśgaḇ ḥômōṯeḵā 'the high fortress of your walls' + hēšaḥ / hišpîl / higgîaʿ lā-ʾāreṣ 'brought down / laid low / brought to the ground'; 2ms addressee (Moab)
entries.literal: and the fortress, the high stronghold of your walls, he has bowed down, laid low, brought to the ground, unto dust
entries.standardEnglish: the high fortress of thy walls hath he brought down, laid low, and brought to the ground, even to the dust (ASV/JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'And the high fortress of your walls he has brought down, laid low, brought to the ground, to the dust' - the 2ms suffix ḥômōṯeḵā 'your walls' addressed directly to Moab (apostrophe); miḇṣar 'fortress' + miśgāḇ 'high stronghold' as a fortified-height pair; the three verbs hēšaḥ (√šḥḥ 'bow down'), hišpîl (√špl 'lay low'), higgîaʿ lā-ʾāreṣ 'brought to the ground' as a demolition-triplet ending ʿaḏ-ʿāp̄ār 'to the dust'.
entries.rationale: The oracle closes on the levelling of Moab's stronghold, apostrophized in the second person: miḇṣar miśgaḇ ḥômōṯeḵā 'the fortress, the high stronghold of your walls' - the 2ms suffix ḥômōṯeḵā 'your walls' addresses Moab directly (the addressee-shift from the 3ms 'Moab' of 25:10-11). miḇṣār 'fortress' and miśgāḇ 'high, inaccessible refuge' form a fortified-height pair (rendered as two stacked nouns, with the hendiadys 'your high fortified walls' recorded as an alternative), and the three piled verbs - hēšaḥ (Hiphil of šḥḥ 'bow down, bring low'), hišpîl (Hiphil of špl 'lay low'), higgîaʿ lā-ʾāreṣ 'brought to the ground' - form a demolition-triplet climaxing in ʿaḏ-ʿāp̄ār 'to the dust' (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39). The renderings are the standard versional values (ASV/JPS) and carry no lens; the entry records the addressee-shift and the demolition-triplet.

entries.source: יוּשַׁר הַשִּׁיר … יְשׁוּעָה יָשִׁית חוֹמוֹת וָחֵל
entries.translit: yûšar haš-šîr … yᵉšûʿāh yāšîṯ ḥômôṯ wā-ḥēl
entries.strongs: H7891 (šîr 'sing'); H3444 (yᵉšûʿāh 'salvation'); H7896 (šîṯ 'set, appoint'); H2346 (ḥômāh 'wall'); H2426 (ḥêl 'rampart, outer wall')
entries.lemma: the song's opening - yûšar 'shall be sung' (Hophal) and yᵉšûʿāh yāšîṯ ḥômôṯ wā-ḥēl 'salvation he sets as walls and rampart'
entries.literal: this song shall be sung … salvation he sets (as) walls and rampart
entries.standardEnglish: salvation will he appoint for walls and bulwarks (ASV); walls and bulwark he appoints for salvation (JPS 1917)
entries.wohChoice: 'he sets salvation as walls and rampart' - yᵉšûʿāh read as the material appointed AS the city's defenses (ASV-aligned); ḥêl 'rampart / outer wall'; the alternative 'walls … he appoints for salvation' (JPS) noted. yûšar 'shall be sung' - the eschatological song of Judah, 'in that day'.
entries.rationale: Chapter 26 opens the eschatological 'song … sung in the land of Judah' with a passive yûšar (Hophal of šîr) 'shall be sung' and celebrates a 'strong city' (ʿîr ʿoz-lānû) whose defenses are YHWH's own yᵉšûʿāh 'salvation'. The syntactic crux is yᵉšûʿāh yāšîṯ ḥômôṯ wā-ḥēl: whether 'salvation' is the material appointed AS the walls and rampart (ASV 'salvation will he appoint for walls and bulwarks') or the walls are appointed FOR salvation (JPS 1917 'walls and bulwark he appoints for salvation'). The Editor ratifies the ASV-aligned reading - salvation itself constitutes the city's fortification, ḥêl being the outer wall or fore-rampart (BDB, HALOT) - the reading that best fits the antithesis with the 'lofty city' brought down to the dust in 26:5. The renderings are standard and carry no lens; the strong-city-of-salvation set against the fallen city of the tyrants is a matter of the song's structure, developed in commentary (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27, Continental, 1997; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39, AB 19, 2000).

entries.strongs: H3336 (yēṣer 'form, framing, inclination'); H5564 (sāmaḵ 'support, sustain'); H5341 (nāṣar 'keep, guard'); H7965 (šālôm)
entries.lemma: yēṣer sāmûḵ 'the steadfast mind / purpose' + the doubled šālôm šālôm
entries.literal: a supported / steadfast disposition you keep (in) peace, peace
entries.standardEnglish: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee (ASV); The mind stayed on Thee Thou keepest in perfect peace (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'the steadfast mind you keep in peace, peace' - yēṣer 'mind / disposition / purpose' (the same noun as Gen 6:5's yēṣer); sāmûḵ 'firmly-supported, steadfast'; the doubled šālôm ׀ šālôm preserved literally on the surface, the intensive idiom 'perfect / complete peace' noted in commentary.
entries.rationale: The verse promises peace to the yēṣer sāmûḵ - yēṣer 'form, framing, inclination, disposition' (the same noun as the yēṣer of Gen 6:5 and 8:21) qualified by sāmûḵ (passive participle of sāmaḵ 'support, sustain'), hence 'a steadfast / firmly-supported mind or purpose'; tiṣṣōr (nāṣar 'keep, guard') 'you keep'. The distinctive feature is the doubled šālôm ׀ šālôm (with paseq), which the Editor preserves literally on the surface as 'peace, peace' rather than collapsing to the intensive idiom 'perfect peace' (KJV/ASV) - the repetition is an emphatic reduplication (a superlative-by-doubling), and keeping the doubling lets the reader see the Hebrew's own emphasis rather than an English paraphrase of it. The intensive 'perfect / complete peace' sense is genuine and is noted in commentary; the renderings are standard and carry no lens (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; BDB, HALOT s.v. yēṣer).

entries.strongs: H3050 (Yāh); H3068 (YHWH); H6697 (ṣûr 'rock'); H5769 (ʿôlām, pl. ʿôlāmîm)
entries.lemma: the short divine name Yāh + the epithet ṣûr ʿôlāmîm 'everlasting rock'
entries.literal: in Yah YHWH (is) a rock of ages / eternities
entries.standardEnglish: for in the LORD JEHOVAH is an everlasting rock (ASV); for the LORD is GOD, an everlasting Rock (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'in Yah YHWH is an everlasting rock' - Yāh transliterated (the short form of the Tetragrammaton) and kept distinct from the YHWH house-style; ṣûr 'rock' rendered plainly as a divine epithet (lower-case, not capitalized as a title); ʿôlāmîm 'ages / eternities' rendered adverbially 'everlasting'.
entries.rationale: The verse pairs the short divine name יָהּ Yāh with the Tetragrammaton (bᵉ-Yāh YHWH) and closes with the epithet ṣûr ʿôlāmîm. Yāh (H3050) is the shortened form of the Tetragrammaton (the element of hallĕlû-Yāh), and the Editor transliterates 'Yah' - kept typographically distinct from the corpus 'YHWH' house-style for the full name - rather than folding it into 'the LORD is GOD' (JPS) or reading a repeated name 'Jehovah, even Jehovah' (ASV), so the reader can see the source's own juxtaposition of the two forms. ṣûr 'rock' (H6697) is a live divine epithet across the corpus (Deut 32:4, 18, 31; Isa 30:29; 2 Sam 22:2-3), and ʿôlāmîm, the plural of ʿôlām 'far-distant time, age', is rendered adverbially 'everlasting' (ʿôlām being durational rather than metaphysical-eternal); the Editor renders 'an everlasting rock' with ṣûr lower-case as an epithet rather than capitalized as a fixed title, the divine-Rock tradition carried in commentary. The renderings are standard and carry no lens (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39).

entries.strongs: H3477 (yāšār 'upright, straight'); H4570 (maʿgāl 'track, path'); H6662 (ṣaddîq); H6424 (pālas 'weigh, make level')
entries.lemma: yāšār as a vocative divine epithet 'O Upright One' + tᵉp̄allēs 'you make level'
entries.literal: (O) upright one, the track of the righteous you weigh-out / make-level
entries.standardEnglish: Thou that art upright dost direct the path of the just (ASV); Thou Most Upright, makest level the path of the righteous (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'O Upright One, you make smooth the path of the righteous' - yāšār taken as a vocative divine epithet (JPS-aligned), against the adjectival 'the path … is straight' (ASV); tᵉp̄allēs 'make level / smooth / weigh out' (pls); committed to no divine-identity lens.
entries.rationale: In yāšār maʿgal ṣaddîq tᵉp̄allēs the word yāšār 'upright, straight, level' (H3477) can be read either as a vocative divine epithet addressed to YHWH ('O Upright One, you make level the track of the righteous', so JPS 'Thou Most Upright') or adjectivally / impersonally as a predicate of the path ('the path of the righteous is straight; you make it level', so ASV). The Editor takes the vocative epithet, which suits the surrounding second-person address to YHWH (26:8-9, 11-12) and the parallel 'O Upright One' construal in the versions, while committing to no divine-identity lens; tᵉp̄allēs (Piel of pālas 'weigh out, make level') is 'you make level / smooth' (the path made straight and passable for the righteous). Both construals are defensible and the adjectival reading is noted; the renderings are standard and carry no lens (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Kaiser, Isaiah 13-39, OTL, 1974; BDB, HALOT s.v. pālas).

entries.strongs: H430 (ʾĕlōhîm, suffixed ʾĕlōhênû); H1166 (bāʿal 'rule, be master over'); H113 (ʾāḏôn, pl. ʾăḏōnîm); H2108 (zûlāh 'besides, except')
entries.lemma: ʾĕlōhênû 'our God' (non-application of 'the Elohim') + ʾăḏōnîm zûlāṯeḵā 'other lords besides you' (human / foreign overlords)
entries.partOfSpeech: divine noun (suffixed 1cp) + noun (plural of ʾāḏôn) + preposition
entries.literal: YHWH our God, lords other than you have ruled / mastered us
entries.standardEnglish: O LORD our God, other lords besides thee have had dominion over us (ASV/JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'O YHWH our God, other lords besides you have ruled over us' - ʾĕlōhênû 'our God' (the corpus 'the Elohim' convention deliberately NOT applied to a suffixed first-person confession, per the 53:4 / 24:15 / 25:1,9 precedent); ʾăḏōnîm zûlāṯeḵā 'other lords / masters besides you' - the plural of ʾāḏôn naming the human / foreign overlords (Assyria, Babylon) who ruled Judah, NOT the divine title Adonai (so adonai-standalone-title-isaiah does not apply); bᵉʿālûnû 'have ruled / been masters over us' (bʿl).
entries.rationale: The verse makes two decisions. (i) ʾĕlōhênû 'our God' (suffixed ʾĕlōhîm) is rendered plainly, and the corpus 'the Elohim' convention (central entry elohim-as-translation, scoped to Genesis 1) is deliberately NOT applied - a suffixed first-person confession ('YHWH our God') does not take the narrative-frame convention, exactly as at Isa 53:4 (mukkēh ʾĕlōhîm 'God'), 24:15 (ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl 'the God of Israel'), and 25:1 / 25:9 ('my God' / 'our God'); ISA-26:13 is therefore NOT added to that central entry's appliesTo. (ii) ʾăḏōnîm zûlāṯeḵā 'lords / masters other than you' is the plural of ʾāḏôn 'lord, master' (H113) naming the human / foreign overlords who have ruled Judah (Assyria, Babylon) - NOT the divine title ʾăḏōnāy 'the Lord' (H136), so the overlay adonai-standalone-title-isaiah entry does not apply and no divine referent is imported; bᵉʿālûnû (bʿl 'rule, be master over', H1166) is 'have ruled / been masters over us'. Both renderings are the standard versional values (ASV/JPS) and carry no lens; the entry records the elohim non-application and the human-overlords reading (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39).

entries.strongs: H7496 (rᵉp̄āʾîm 'shades, the dead'); cf. H7497 (rᵉp̄āʾîm 'Rephaim', the giant peoples)
entries.lemma: rᵉp̄āʾîm in the 'shades / the dead' sense (the underworld dead), distinct from the homonymous giant-people Rephaim
entries.partOfSpeech: noun (masculine plural) - the shades of the dead
entries.literal: shades / the powerless dead (26:14) … shades (26:19)
entries.standardEnglish: the deceased (ASV); the shades (JPS/NRSV)
entries.wohChoice: 'the shades' / 'the dead' - rᵉp̄āʾîm rendered in its 'shades of the dead' sense (the denizens of Sheol) at BOTH 26:14 (the shades that 'do not rise') and 26:19 (the shades the earth gives up ALIVE, the inverse); the giant-warrior sense (central refaim-giant-peoples and nephilim-giants-1-enoch-7-gen-6-4-cross-corpus entries) deliberately NOT applied; the homonymy with the Ugaritic rpʾum and the biblical giant-Rephaim carried in commentary, not the line.
entries.rationale: rᵉp̄āʾîm occurs twice in the chapter, both in its 'shades / the dead' sense - the powerless denizens of Sheol (H7496): at 26:14 'the shades do not rise' (rᵉp̄āʾîm bal-yāqumû, the dead 'other lords' declared impotent) and at 26:19 'the earth will give birth to the shades' (wā-ʾāreṣ rᵉp̄āʾîm tappîl, the same dead given up alive - the deliberate inverse of 26:14). This is the same lexeme as, and is homonymous / etymologically entangled with, the giant-people Rephaim of Gen 14:5 and Deut 2-3 and the Ugaritic rpʾum (the divinized heroic dead), but the two senses form 'a separate philological track' (the words of the central refaim-giant-peoples entry's own rationale, which explicitly cites Isa 14:9, 26:14, and 26:19 as the shades-sense); BDB and HALOT track the giants and the shades as a single lemma while distinguishing the senses. Accordingly, neither the central refaim-giant-peoples entry (the pre-Israelite giant peoples) nor the central nephilim-giants-1-enoch-7-gen-6-4-cross-corpus entry (the antediluvian giant-warrior chain) is applied to ISA-26:14 or 26:19 - applying a giant-Rephaim / Nephilim entry to the 'shades' sense would be a lens-and-lexical error, since the shades here are the ordinary dead, not warriors or giants. The Editor renders 'the shades' / 'the dead' (ASV 'the deceased'; JPS/NRSV 'the shades'), the standard and consensus rendering; the giant-Rephaim / Ugaritic rpʾum homonymy is carried in commentary, not the line, and the entry is direct (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; L'Heureux, Rank Among the Canaanite Gods, 1979; Pope, Job, AB, 1965; J. Day, God's Conflict with the Dragon and the Sea, 1985).

entries.strongs: H6693 (ṣûq 'pour out, be in straits'); H3908 (laḥaš 'whisper, charm, incantation'); H4148 (mûsār 'discipline, chastening')
entries.lemma: the difficult ṣāqûn laḥaš 'they poured out a whisper(ed prayer)' + mûsārḵā lāmô 'your chastening upon them'
entries.literal: they poured out a whisper … your discipline (was) to / upon them
entries.standardEnglish: they poured out a prayer when thy chastening was upon them (ASV); silently they poured out a prayer (NJPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'they poured out a whispered prayer when your chastening was upon them' - ṣāqûn (anomalous, best from ṣûq 'pour out, be in straits') 'they poured out'; laḥaš 'a whispered prayer' (the hushed-prayer sense, JPS), against the 'charm / incantation' and 'cried out in a whisper' senses; mûsārḵā lāmô 'your chastening upon them'; the colon flagged as textually hard.
entries.rationale: The colon ṣāqûn laḥaš is textually hard. ṣāqûn is an anomalous verb form best derived from ṣûq 'pour out, be in straits, be distressed' (giving 'they poured out'), with a minority tie to ṣāʿaq 'cry out'; laḥaš (H3908) is 'a whisper', used both of a hushed prayer and of a magical charm or incantation (cf. Isa 3:3 'skilled in charms'; Eccl 10:11; Ps 58:6). The Editor renders 'they poured out a whispered prayer' - the hushed-petition sense (JPS 'silently they poured out a prayer'), which fits the context of Judah seeking YHWH 'in distress' (baṣṣar) under his chastening (mûsārḵā, mûsār 'discipline, chastening', H4148), against the 'charm / incantation' and 'cried out in a whisper' construals, which are noted. The renderings are standard, the difficulty of the colon is flagged, and no lens is carried (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39; BDB, HALOT s.v. laḥaš).

entries.translit: yāladnû rûaḥ yᵉšûʿōṯ bal-naʿăśeh ʾereṣ û-ḇal-yippᵉlû yōšᵉḇê ṯēḇēl
entries.strongs: H3205 (yālaḏ 'bear, bring forth'); H7307 (rûaḥ 'wind, breath'); H3444 (yᵉšûʿāh, pl. yᵉšûʿōṯ); H6213 (ʿāśāh); H5307 (nāp̄al 'fall'); H8398 (tēḇēl 'world')
entries.lemma: yāladnû rûaḥ 'we gave birth to wind' + the yᵉšûʿōṯ 'deliverances' and yippᵉlû (nāp̄al) 'come to birth / fall' cruxes
entries.literal: we gave birth to wind; deliverances we do not accomplish (in) the earth, and the inhabitants of the world do not fall / come-to-birth
entries.standardEnglish: we have as it were brought forth wind; we have not wrought any deliverance in the earth, neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen (ASV); the inhabitants of the world have not come to life (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'as if we gave birth to wind. We have wrought no deliverance in the earth, and the inhabitants of the world have not come to birth' - yᵉšûʿōṯ plural 'deliverances / victories'; yippᵉlû (nāp̄al 'fall') read as 'come to birth' in continuity with the childbirth-metaphor of 26:17-19 (JPS), against the 'have not fallen / been overthrown' reading (ASV); the fall / overthrow alternative flagged.
entries.rationale: The verse extends the childbirth simile of 26:17: the people 'gave birth to wind' (yāladnû rûaḥ) - labor that produced nothing. Two cruxes follow. (i) yᵉšûʿōṯ bal-naʿăśeh ʾereṣ is the terse 'we have wrought no deliverance(s) in the earth', yᵉšûʿōṯ being the plural of yᵉšûʿāh 'deliverance, victory'. (ii) û-ḇal yippᵉlû yōšᵉḇê ṯēḇēl turns on yippᵉlû (nāp̄al 'fall'): either 'the inhabitants of the world have not fallen / been overthrown' (ASV), or, continuing the birth-metaphor of the verse, 'the inhabitants of the world have not come to birth / are not born' (JPS). The Editor takes the childbirth reading, consistent with the birth-imagery running through 26:17-19 (conceive, writhe, give birth) and anticipating tappîl 'give birth' at 26:19, with the 'fall / overthrow' alternative flagged; the renderings are standard and carry no lens (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Kaiser, Isaiah 13-39, OTL; BDB, HALOT s.v. nāp̄al).

entries.translit: yiḥyû mēṯeḵā nᵉḇēlāṯî yᵉqûmûn … wā-ʾāreṣ rᵉp̄āʾîm tappîl
entries.strongs: H2421 (ḥāyāh 'live'); H4191 (māweṯ, part. mēṯîm 'dead'); H5038 (nᵉḇēlāh 'corpse, carcass'); H6965 (qûm 'arise'); H5307 (nāp̄al, Hiphil tappîl 'cause to fall / bring forth')
entries.lemma: the resurrection line - yiḥyû mēṯeḵā 'your dead shall live', nᵉḇēlāṯî yᵉqûmûn 'my corpses shall rise' (the number crux), and wā-ʾāreṣ rᵉp̄āʾîm tappîl (the tappîl 'give birth / cast forth' crux)
entries.partOfSpeech: resurrection-language clause + number-agreement crux + Hiphil-verb crux
entries.literal: your dead shall live; my corpse(s), they shall arise … and the earth, the shades it shall cause-to-fall / bring-forth
entries.standardEnglish: Thy dead shall live; my dead bodies shall arise … and the earth shall cast forth the dead (ASV); the earth shall bring to life the shades (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'Your dead shall live; my corpses shall rise … and the earth will give birth to the shades' - the MT surface rendered plainly; nᵉḇēlāṯî (1cs singular 'my corpse') paired with yᵉqûmûn (3mp) rendered collectively 'my corpses shall rise', retaining the MT against the emendation nᵉḇēlāṯām 'their bodies' (NRSV/RSV); tappîl (Hiphil of nāp̄al) rendered 'give birth to' in continuity with the childbirth-imagery of 26:17-18, the ASV/KJV 'cast forth / cast out' noted as the equal alternative. The bodily-resurrection reading and the cross-corpus link to Dan 12:2 and Ezek 37 are apparatus-only (central resurrection-dan-12-2-3-foundational-cross-corpus, appliesTo extended to ISA-26:19).
entries.rationale: This is the chapter's marquee line and the clearest resurrection-language text in Isaiah: yiḥyû mēṯeḵā 'your dead shall live', nᵉḇēlāṯî yᵉqûmûn 'my corpse(s) shall rise', hāqîṣû wᵉrannᵉnû šōḵᵉnê ʿāp̄ār 'awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust'. The Editor renders the Masoretic surface plainly - 'your dead shall live' is grammatically explicit and carries no lens, so the entry is direct; whether the raising is literal individual bodily resurrection or a national / corporate-restoration metaphor (the dead-nation revived, as in Ezek 37) is left OPEN on the surface and NOT pre-resolved, per accuracy-before-lens. The bodily-resurrection reading and the cross-corpus link - Dan 12:2, the Hebrew Bible's first unambiguous individual-eschatological resurrection, and Ezek 37, the dry-bones corporate resurrection - are the interpretive layer, developed in commentary and recorded via the central resurrection-dan-12-2-3-foundational-cross-corpus entry, whose own source field names Isa 26:19 'the prophetic-resurrection fountainhead' and whose appliesTo is extended to ISA-26:19 by orchestrator diff; that central entry's lens-discipline (no bodily-resurrection-of-all pre-resolution; the corporate / individual question kept open) governs. Two form-decisions: nᵉḇēlāṯî is formally 1cs singular 'my corpse' (nᵉḇēlāh 'carcass, corpse', H5038) but pairs with yᵉqûmûn (3mp 'they shall arise'), and is rendered collectively 'my corpses shall rise', retaining the Masoretic reading against the widely-proposed emendation nᵉḇēlāṯām 'their bodies' (adopted by NRSV/RSV); tappîl (Hiphil of nāp̄al 'cause to fall', H5307) governs wā-ʾāreṣ … rᵉp̄āʾîm and is rendered 'the earth will give birth to the shades', tying the verb to the childbirth-imagery of 26:17-18 (so NRSV 'the earth will give birth'; JPS 'bring to life'), with the ASV/KJV 'cast forth / cast out' (the earth or Sheol disgorging its dead) noted as the equal alternative. The renderings are within the standard scholarly range and the entry is direct, the eschatological program confined to the apparatus (J. Day, God's Conflict with the Dragon and the Sea, 1985; J. D. Levenson, Resurrection and the Restoration of Israel, 2006; Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39).

entries.strongs: H2919 (ṭal 'dew'); H219 (ʾôrāh, pl. ʾôrōṯ 'lights'); cf. ʾôrōṯ 'herbs, mallows' (2 Kgs 4:39)
entries.lemma: ṭal ʾôrōṯ 'a dew of lights' - the ʾôrōṯ 'lights' vs homograph 'herbs / mallows' crux
entries.literal: for a dew of lights (is) your dew
entries.standardEnglish: thy dew is as the dew of herbs (ASV/KJV); your dew is a dew of light (NRSV); a dew on fresh growth (NJPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'for your dew is a dew of lights' - ʾôrōṯ read as 'lights' (luminous / celestial, life-giving dew - NRSV 'dew of light'), against the homograph ʾôrōṯ 'herbs / mallows' (the plant-reviving dew, ASV/KJV 'dew of herbs', cf. 2 Kgs 4:39); the 'lights' reading retained, the 'herbs' reading noted.
entries.rationale: The line kî ṭal ʾôrōṯ ṭalleḵā 'for your dew is a dew of ʾôrōṯ' turns on the crux ʾôrōṯ. Read as the plural of ʾôrāh 'light' (H219; cf. Ps 139:12), it gives 'a dew of lights' - a luminous, celestial, life-giving dew (NRSV 'a dew of light'), the reading the Editor retains; read as the homograph ʾôrōṯ 'herbs, mallows' (the greens gathered in 2 Kgs 4:39), it gives 'a dew of herbs' - a dew that revives vegetation (ASV/KJV 'dew of herbs'). The Editor keeps 'a dew of lights', which suits the resurrection / awakening context (the dew as the agent that quickens the dead who 'dwell in the dust'), with the 'herbs' reading disclosed for the reader's audit; both are defensible and the choice carries no lens beyond the vivifying-dew image the verse itself supplies. The renderings are standard and the entry is direct (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39; BDB, HALOT s.v. ʾôrāh).

entries.translit: ûsᵉḡōr dᵉlāṯeḵā(ketiv) / dᵉlāṯḵā(qere) baʿăḏeḵā … ʿaḏ-yaʿăḇôr(ketiv) / yaʿăḇār(qere) zāʿam
entries.strongs: H1817 (deleṯ 'door'); H5674 (ʿāḇar 'pass over'); H2195 (zaʿam 'indignation, wrath'); H2247 (ḥāḇāh 'hide')
entries.lemma: two ketiv/qere pairs at 26:20 - dᵉlāṯeḵā / dᵉlāṯḵā 'your doors / door' and yaʿăḇôr / yaʿăḇār 'passes'; with ḥăḇî 'hide yourself' and zaʿam 'indignation'
entries.literal: shut your door(s) behind you … until the indignation passes
entries.standardEnglish: shut thy doors about thee … until the indignation be overpast (ASV); shut thy door behind thee (JPS, qere)
entries.wohChoice: 'shut your door behind you … until the indignation passes over' - the qere translated in both pairs (dᵉlāṯḵā 'your door' sg.; yaʿăḇār 'passes'), per the qere-first structural-preservation rule, with the ketiv (dᵉlāṯeḵā 'your doors' pl.; yaʿăḇôr) preserved in the source and noted; ḥăḇî 'hide yourself'; zaʿam 'indignation, wrath' (YHWH's wrath of 26:21).
entries.rationale: Verse 20 carries two ketiv/qere pairs. (i) דלתיך (ketiv dᵉlāṯeḵā 'your doors', plural) / דְּלָתְךָ (qere dᵉlāṯḵā 'your door', singular) in ûsᵉḡōr … baʿăḏeḵā 'and shut your door(s) behind you'. (ii) יעבור (ketiv yaʿăḇôr) / יַעֲבָר (qere yaʿăḇār) in ʿaḏ- … zāʿam 'until the indignation passes'. Per the project's ketiv/qere structural-preservation convention the qere is translated ('your door' singular; 'passes over') and the ketiv is preserved verbatim in the source text and noted; the difference is orthographic / morphological and non-substantive. ḥăḇî (ḥāḇāh 'hide', H2247) 'hide yourself' and zaʿam 'indignation, wrath' (H2195) frame the summons to the people to shelter 'for a little moment' until YHWH's wrath - the wrath that in 26:21 falls on the inhabitants of the earth - has passed over, a sheltering-until-the-wrath-passes motif noted in commentary (cf. Exod 12:22-23). The renderings are standard and carry no lens (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39).

entries.translit: liwyāṯān nāḥāš bāriaḥ … liwyāṯān nāḥāš ʿăqallāṯôn … hat-tannîn ʾăšer bay-yām
entries.strongs: H3882 (liwyāṯān); H5175 (nāḥāš); H1281 (bāriaḥ 'fleeing'); H6129 (ʿăqallāṯôn 'crooked, twisting'); H8577 (tannîn); H2719 (ḥereḇ 'sword'); H6485 (pāqad 'punish')
entries.lemma: the chaoskampf serpent-cluster of Isa 27:1 — liwyāṯān (Leviathan) with the epithet-pair nāḥāš bāriaḥ 'fleeing serpent' / nāḥāš ʿăqallāṯôn 'twisting serpent' and hat-tannîn 'the dragon that is in the sea', struck by YHWH's ḥereḇ qāšāh gᵉḏôlāh ḥăzāqāh 'hard, great, and strong sword'
entries.partOfSpeech: proper noun + epithet-pair (noun + adjective) + noun — chaos-serpent combat vocabulary
entries.literal: Leviathan the fleeing/gliding serpent … Leviathan the twisting/writhing serpent … the dragon that is in the sea
entries.standardEnglish: leviathan the swift serpent, and leviathan the crooked serpent; and he will slay the monster that is in the sea (ASV); Leviathan the slant serpent, and Leviathan the tortuous serpent; and He will slay the dragon that is in the sea (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'Leviathan the fleeing serpent, and Leviathan the twisting serpent … the dragon that is in the sea' — proper-noun 'Leviathan' (governed by the central leviathan entry, appliesTo extended to ISA-27:1); nāḥāš 'serpent'; bāriaḥ 'fleeing' (over ASV 'swift', JPS 'slant'); ʿăqallāṯôn 'twisting' (over ASV 'crooked', JPS 'tortuous'); hat-tannîn 'the dragon' (the KJV/JPS dragon-register, governed by the central taninim entry, appliesTo extended to ISA-27:1 — the singular and article follow the source, over ASV 'monster'). NO cross-corpus or lens freight is carried in the line: the Ugaritic Baal-Cycle Lôtanu (bṯn brḥ / bṯn ʿqltn) parallel and the Wheel of Heaven Theomachy-convergence synthesis are apparatus-only.
entries.rationale: Isa 27:1 is the Hebrew Bible's clearest surviving chaoskampf and the flagship cross-corpus site of the chapter: 'in that day YHWH will punish (yip̄qōḏ), with his hard and great and strong sword (ḥereḇ qāšāh gᵉḏôlāh ḥăzāqāh), liwyāṯān nāḥāš bāriaḥ and liwyāṯān nāḥāš ʿăqallāṯôn, and will slay hat-tannîn ʾăšer bay-yām.' Every element is rendered at the standard PD surface and carries no lens: liwyāṯān is the proper noun 'Leviathan' (central leviathan entry, whose own rationale already names Isa 27:1 as 'the critical cross-reference' identifying Leviathan with the tannin — its appliesTo is extended to ISA-27:1 by orchestrator diff); the two epithets are rendered 'fleeing serpent' (bāriaḥ, √brḥ 'flee') and 'twisting serpent' (ʿăqallāṯôn, √ʿql 'be crooked, wind'), the values that best match the Ugaritic cognates, with the ASV 'swift/crooked' and JPS 'slant/tortuous' recorded as alternatives; and hat-tannîn is 'the dragon' (the KJV/JPS dragon-register governed by the central taninim entry, appliesTo extended to ISA-27:1 — the Isa 27:1 singular/definite 'the dragon' is the same dragon-register decision the taninim entry defends against the softening 'sea-monster/serpent' of ASV and the moderns, differing from the Gen 1:21 'great dragons' only in the number and article the source dictates). The Ugaritic Baal Cycle names the identical monster with the identical two epithets: in ʿAnatu's boast (KTU 1.3 III 40-42) and Môtu's speech (KTU 1.5 I 1-3) Baʿlu's slain adversary is ltn (Lôtanu / Litan), bṯn brḥ 'fleeing serpent' and bṯn ʿqltn 'twisting serpent', šlyṭ d šbʿt rʾašm 'tyrant with seven heads'; Hebrew nāḥāš bāriaḥ / nāḥāš ʿăqallāṯôn is the word-for-word cognate of Ugaritic bṯn brḥ / bṯn ʿqltn, and liwyāṯān is the cognate of ltn (both from proto-Semitic √lwy 'coil, wind') — among the most precise Ugaritic-Hebrew matches in the corpus (J. Day, God's Conflict with the Dragon and the Sea, 1985; the central lotanu-leviathan-seven-headed-serpent-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible and chaoskampf-sea-conflict-cross-corpus-ugaritic-akkadian-hebrew-bible entries, whose appliesTo are extended to ISA-27:1 by orchestrator diff, document the cluster; the Hebrew is treated as the cognate in the apparatus, and no Ugaritic vocalization is imported into the Hebrew line). The demythologization-vs-cosmogonic-combat debate is preserved in the apparatus, not the line: Day 1985 reads a live Northwest-Semitic combat-myth inherited by the Hebrew Bible, while D. Tsumura (Creation and Destruction, 2005) is the sober counter-voice, reading the Hebrew attestations as rhetorical-poetic redeployment of inherited imagery. bay-yām 'in the sea' is the merely-locative common noun (the dragon's habitat), NOT the deified Sea; the central yamm-yammu-sea-deified-cross-corpus-chaoskampf-hebrew-bible entry is therefore deliberately NOT applied to this refId (referent mismatch, an accuracy-before-lens non-extension). The broader Wheel of Heaven Theomachy-convergence synthesis — reading Isaiah's serpent alongside Ugaritic Lôtanu, Babylonian Tiamat, and the Indo-European dragon-cycles as convergent memories of conflict among the Elohim — goes beyond both the verse and the comparative philology; it is confined to the per-verse commentary as a hedged, framework-level interpretive layer and is flagged for human sign-off in the editor report. The entry is direct: the wohChoice and the line commit only to the plain PD surface (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27, Continental, 1997; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39, AB 19, 2000; Kaiser, Isaiah 13-39, OTL, 1974).

entries.strongs: H3754 (kerem 'vineyard'); H2531 (ḥemed 'desire, delight'); H2561 (ḥemer 'wine'); H6030 (ʿānāh 'answer, sing')
entries.lemma: kerem ḥemed 'a pleasant vineyard / vineyard of delight' — the opening of the vineyard-song (27:2-6), the redemptive inversion of Isa 5:1-7; with the 1QIsaᵃ ḥemer 'wine' variant and the antiphonal ʿannû-lāh 'sing of it'
entries.literal: a vineyard of delight — sing of it / answer to her
entries.standardEnglish: A vineyard of wine, sing ye unto it (ASV, following ḥemer); In that day sing ye of her: 'A vineyard of delight' (JPS, ḥemed)
entries.wohChoice: 'a pleasant vineyard — sing of it' — MT ḥemed 'delight / pleasant' retained (with the 1QIsaᵃ ḥemer 'wine' variant, adopted by ASV, disclosed for audit); ʿannû-lāh 'sing of it' (ʿnh in the antiphonal 'sing / respond' sense), the feminine suffix pointing to the vineyard. The Isa 5:1-7 vineyard-inversion is carried in commentary; the central kerem-vineyard entry (Gen-9:20-scoped bare lexeme) is cross-referenced but deliberately NOT extended.
entries.rationale: The vineyard-song of 27:2-6 opens with kerem ḥemed 'a pleasant vineyard / vineyard of delight' (ḥemed, √ḥmd 'desire, delight') and the imperative ʿannû-lāh 'sing of it' (ʿnh in its antiphonal 'sing, respond' sense, cf. Exod 15:21; Num 21:17), the feminine suffix -lāh referring to the vineyard. The colon carries a well-known text-critical variant: MT reads חֶמֶד ḥemed 'delight', while 1QIsaᵃ (and the tradition behind ASV 'a vineyard of wine') reads חֶמֶר ḥemer 'wine' — a near-homograph confusion of ד/ר, the two letters being all but identical in the square script. The project translates the Masoretic text and so retains ḥemed 'a pleasant vineyard', disclosing the scroll's ḥemer for the reader's audit; both readings are old and the choice is genuinely open, but accuracy-before-lens keeps the received consonantal text. The song is the deliberate redemptive inversion of the Song of the Vineyard at Isa 5:1-7 (the same kerem lexeme, central kerem-vineyard entry): there YHWH's vineyard yielded wild grapes and was stripped and trampled; here YHWH keeps and waters it and it fills the world with fruit — a thematic reversal developed in commentary and not surfaced in the line. The central kerem-vineyard entry is a Genesis-9:20-scoped bare-lexeme entry (wohChoice 'vineyard'), not a designated cross-corpus keyword; it is cross-referenced here for the shared vineyard-motif (its own rationale names the Isa 5 Song of the Vineyard) but is deliberately NOT extended to ISA-27:2, to avoid over-coupling a Genesis entry to Isaiah for the common nom 'vineyard'. The renderings are standard and carry no lens (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39; Kaiser, Isaiah 13-39, OTL).

entries.strongs: H5341 (nāṣar 'keep, guard'); H8248 (šāqāh 'give drink, water'); H7281 (regaʿ 'moment'); H6485 (pāqad 'visit, punish')
entries.lemma: nōṣᵉrāh 'its keeper' + li-rᵉḡāʿîm ʾašqennāh 'every moment I water it' + the subject-less pen yip̄qōḏ ʿālehā 'lest [any] visit / harm it' (pqd, echoing yip̄qōḏ 'will punish' of 27:1)
entries.partOfSpeech: participle (keeper) + verbal clause + purposive clause with unexpressed subject
entries.literal: I YHWH am its keeper; every moment I water it; lest [any] visit / punish against it, night and day I guard it
entries.standardEnglish: I Jehovah am its keeper; I will water it every moment: lest any hurt it, I will keep it night and day (ASV); Lest Mine anger visit it, I water it every moment (JPS, supplying 'anger')
entries.wohChoice: 'I, YHWH, am its keeper; every moment I water it; lest any harm it, night and day I guard it' — the indefinite-subject reading of yip̄qōḏ (ASV: the received text has no expressed subject), against JPS's supplied 'anger' and the YHWH-as-subject reading; the pqd verb deliberately echoes the yip̄qōḏ 'will punish' of 27:1, now turned protective, a link noted in commentary.
entries.rationale: In the vineyard-song YHWH declares himself nōṣᵉrāh 'its keeper' (nāṣar 'keep, guard'), watering it li-rᵉḡāʿîm 'every moment' (regaʿ 'moment, instant'; ʾašqennāh from šqh 'give drink, irrigate'), and guarding it 'night and day'. The one open decision is the subject of pen yip̄qōḏ ʿālehā 'lest [X] visit / harm against it': the verb (pqd, the same root as yip̄qōḏ 'will punish' in 27:1) has no expressed subject, and the readings span an indefinite subject 'lest any harm it' (ASV), a supplied 'anger' 'lest my wrath visit it' (JPS), and YHWH himself 'lest I punish it'. The translation takes the indefinite reading 'lest any harm it', which stays closest to the received text (which supplies no subject) and avoids importing either the divine wrath JPS reads or a self-directed punishment; accuracy-before-lens forbids resolving a subject the Hebrew leaves open. The deliberate re-use of pqd — the verb that in 27:1 falls in judgment on Leviathan now stands guard over the vineyard — is a literary link noted in commentary, not surfaced in the line. The renderings are standard and carry no lens (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39).

entries.translit: ḥēmāh ʾên lî mî-yittᵉnēnî šāmîr šayiṯ bam-milḥāmāh ʾep̄śᵉʿāh ḇāh ʾăṣîṯennāh yāḥaḏ
entries.strongs: H2534 (ḥēmāh 'wrath, heat'); H8068 (šāmîr 'brier'); H7898 (šayiṯ 'thorn'); H6585 (pāśaʿ 'step, stride'); H3341 (yāṣaṯ 'kindle, burn')
entries.lemma: the dense crux of 27:4 — ḥēmāh ʾên lî 'I have no wrath'; the optative idiom mî-yittᵉnēnî 'would that I had'; šāmîr wā-šayiṯ 'briers and thorns'; ʾep̄śᵉʿāh 'I would stride against'; ʾăṣîṯennāh yāḥaḏ 'I would burn it all together'
entries.partOfSpeech: verbless clause + optative idiom + two verbs (crux) with ambiguous feminine-suffix antecedents
entries.literal: wrath I have none; who will give me briers and thorns in battle — I would stride into it, I would burn it all together
entries.standardEnglish: Wrath is not in me: would that the briers and thorns were against me in battle! I would march upon them, I would burn them together (ASV); I have no wall; would that I were as the briers and thorns in flame! (JPS, a divergent construal)
entries.wohChoice: 'I have no wrath. Would that I had briers and thorns to face in battle! I would stride against them, I would set them ablaze all together' — YHWH disclaims wrath toward the vineyard but would wage war on any briers and thorns that would infest it; the optative mî-yittᵉnēnî 'would that I had'; the feminine suffixes (ḇāh, ʾăṣîṯennāh) read as the thorn-mass (ASV/JPS-leaning), not the vineyard.
entries.rationale: 27:4 is a genuine scholarly crux. ḥēmāh ʾên lî is 'I have no wrath / fury' (ḥēmāh, the heat of anger). mî-yittᵉnēnî šāmîr šayiṯ bam-milḥāmāh, literally 'who will give me briers and thorns in battle', is the standard Hebrew optative idiom (mî-yittēn 'who will give' = 'would that'), here 'would that I had briers and thorns to fight' — YHWH, having no wrath against the vineyard itself, wishes for an enemy (the briers and thorns that would choke it) to march against. ʾep̄śᵉʿāh (√pśʿ 'step, stride') is 'I would stride / march against', and ʾăṣîṯennāh yāḥaḏ (√yṣt 'kindle, set on fire') 'I would burn it all together'. The antecedents of the feminine suffixes (ḇāh 'into/against it', -ennāh 'it') are ambiguous — the vineyard or the thorn-mass — and the whole verse's sense turns on it; the translation follows the ASV/JPS construal in which YHWH wars on the thorns, not the vineyard, reading the suffixes as the thorn-mass, with the harsher construal (YHWH marching into and burning the vineyard) and JPS's quite different 'would that I were as the briers and thorns in flame' recorded as alternatives. The renderings are within the standard scholarly range and carry no lens; the entry records the optative idiom and the suffix-antecedent crux (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Kaiser, Isaiah 13-39, OTL; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39).

entries.source: אוֹ יַחֲזֵק בְּמָעוּזִּי יַעֲשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם לִי שָׁלוֹם יַעֲשֶׂה־לִּי
entries.translit: ʾô yaḥăzēq bᵉ-māʿûzzî yaʿăśeh šālôm lî šālôm yaʿăśeh-lî
entries.strongs: H4581 (māʿôz 'stronghold, refuge, protection'); H2388 (ḥāzaq 'be strong, take hold'); H7965 (šālôm 'peace')
entries.lemma: māʿôz 'stronghold / refuge / protection' + the peace-offer: let the adversary take hold of YHWH's protection and make peace with him (the doubled šālôm)
entries.literal: or let him take hold of my stronghold, let him make peace with me; peace let him make with me
entries.standardEnglish: Or else let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me; yea, let him make peace with me (ASV/JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'Or let him take hold of my stronghold, that he may make peace with me; peace let him make with me' — māʿôz 'stronghold' (with 'refuge / protection' as equivalents); the doubled 'peace let him make with me' preserved as the source has it; the offer of refuge and peace held out to the one who lays hold of YHWH's protection.
entries.rationale: The verse offers terms of peace: ʾô yaḥăzēq bᵉ-māʿûzzî 'or let him take hold of my stronghold' (māʿôz 'place of safety, stronghold, refuge, protection', √ʿzz 'be strong'; ḥzq 'take hold'), yaʿăśeh šālôm lî 'let him make peace with me', with the emphatic repetition šālôm yaʿăśeh-lî 'peace let him make with me'. The only open point is the rendering of māʿôz — 'stronghold' (the concrete fortified refuge), 'refuge', or 'protection' — and the translation keeps 'stronghold' (ASV/JPS 'strength/stronghold') with the others as equivalents; the sense is otherwise standard. The doubled šālôm is preserved on the surface rather than collapsed into an intensive. The image — the adversary invited to seize hold of YHWH's own protection and so come to terms — is a matter of the verse's sense, and the renderings carry no lens (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39; BDB, HALOT s.v. māʿôz).

entries.translit: ha-kᵉmakkaṯ makkēhû hikkāhû ʾim-kᵉhereḡ hăruḡāyw hōrāḡ
entries.strongs: H5221 (nāḵāh 'strike, smite'); H2026 (hāraḡ 'slay, kill')
entries.lemma: the rhetorical double-question of measured judgment — has YHWH struck Israel as he struck Israel's strikers? was Israel slain as its slayers were slain?
entries.partOfSpeech: double rhetorical question (two paronomastic clauses) with ambiguous pronoun-referents
entries.literal: as the striking of the one who struck him did he strike him? or as the slaying of his slain was he slain?
entries.standardEnglish: Hath he smitten him as he smote those that smote him? or is he slain according to the slaughter of them that were slain by him? (ASV); Was he beaten as the beating of him that beat him? (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'Has he struck him as he struck the one who struck him? Or was he slain as his slain were slain?' — the ambiguous pronoun-referents left as the Hebrew leaves them; the measured-judgment reading (Israel was not punished as harshly as its oppressors) kept for commentary, not resolved in the line.
entries.rationale: 27:7 is a double rhetorical question built on two paronomastic clauses: ha-kᵉmakkaṯ makkēhû hikkāhû 'has he struck him with the stroke of the one who struck him?' (root nkh 'strike', three times) and ʾim-kᵉhereḡ hăruḡāyw hōrāḡ 'or was he slain with the slaying of his slain?' (root hrg 'slay', three times). The 'he/him' subjects and objects are unnamed and the referents are a genuine crux — the standard reading takes YHWH as the striker throughout and contrasts the measured blow he dealt Israel with the heavier blow he dealt Israel's oppressors: Israel was NOT struck or slain as severely as those who struck and slew Israel. The translation renders the questions plainly and leaves the referents as the Hebrew leaves them, keeping the measured-judgment argument for commentary rather than resolving the pronouns in the line (accuracy-before-lens). The renderings are standard and carry no lens (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Kaiser, Isaiah 13-39, OTL; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39).

entries.source: בְּסַּאסְּאָה בְּשַׁלְחָהּ תְּרִיבֶנָּה הָגָה בְּרוּחוֹ הַקָּשָׁה בְּיוֹם קָדִים
entries.translit: bᵉsaʾsᵉʾāh bᵉšallᵉḥāh tᵉrîḇennāh hāḡāh bᵉrûḥô ha-qāšāh bᵉyôm qāḏîm
entries.strongs: H5432 (saʾsᵉʾāh — hapax, related to sᵉʾāh 'measure'); H7971 (šālaḥ 'send away'); H7378 (rîḇ 'contend'); H1898 (hāḡāh 'remove, mutter'); H7307 (rûaḥ 'wind, blast'); H6921 (qāḏîm 'east wind')
entries.lemma: the hapax bᵉsaʾsᵉʾāh 'in measure' crux + bᵉšallᵉḥāh 'by sending her away' (šlḥ, divorce/exile register) + tᵉrîḇennāh 'you contend with her' + hāḡāh 'he removed [her]' + rûaḥ qāšāh 'harsh blast' + yôm qāḏîm 'the day of the east wind'; the 2nd->3rd person shift
entries.partOfSpeech: hapax adverbial (crux) + verbal clauses with a person-shift
entries.literal: in measure, in sending her away, you contend with her; he drove [her] away with his harsh wind in the day of the east wind
entries.standardEnglish: In measure, when thou sendest her away, thou dost contend with her; he hath removed her with his rough blast in the day of the east wind (ASV); Thou didst contend with them in full measure, sending them away (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'In measure, by sending her away, you contend with her; he removed her with his harsh blast in the day of the east wind' — bᵉsaʾsᵉʾāh taken from sᵉʾāh 'measure' (JPS 'In full measure'), against the 'by driving away' derivation; bᵉšallᵉḥāh 'by sending her away' (šlḥ, the divorce/exile register); the 2nd->3rd person shift ('you contend' -> 'he removed') preserved rather than normalized; yôm qāḏîm the scorching east-wind sirocco.
entries.rationale: 27:8 is one of the hardest verses in the chapter. bᵉsaʾsᵉʾāh (בְּסַּאסְּאָה) is a hapax: the majority derive it by reduplication from sᵉʾāh 'measure' (so 'in measure / in full measure', JPS), against a minority root sense 'drive / scare away' ('by driving her away'); the LXX and other versions diverge further. The translation takes the 'measure' derivation, which fits the measured-judgment argument of vv7-9. bᵉšallᵉḥāh (šlḥ 'send away') is 'by / when sending her away', carrying a possible divorce or exile register; tᵉrîḇennāh (rîḇ 'contend, bring suit') 'you contend with her'; hāḡāh (a rare use of hgh, here 'remove, drive away') 'he removed / drove her away'; bᵉrûḥô ha-qāšāh 'with his harsh wind / blast'; and bᵉyôm qāḏîm 'in the day of the east wind' — the scorching sirocco that withers vegetation (cf. Hos 13:15; Jonah 4:8). The verse also shifts from the second person ('you contend') to the third ('he removed') mid-clause; the translation preserves the shift rather than normalizing it to a single subject, since the Hebrew's own alternation is a datum, not an error to be smoothed. The renderings are within the standard scholarly range and carry no lens; the entry records the hapax crux, the person-shift, and the east-wind image (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39; Kaiser, Isaiah 13-39, OTL; BDB, HALOT).

entries.translit: kol-ʾaḇnê mizbēaḥ kᵉ-ʾaḇnê-ḡir mᵉnuppāṣôṯ lō-yāqumû ʾăšērîm wᵉ-ḥammānîm
entries.strongs: H842 (ʾăšērāh, pl. ʾăšērîm); H2553 (ḥammān 'sun-pillar, incense-altar'); H4196 (mizbēaḥ 'altar'); H1615 (gir 'chalk, lime'); H5310 (nāp̄aṣ 'shatter')
entries.lemma: the cult-purge inventory of 27:9 — the altar-stones 'like crushed chalkstones' + ʾăšērîm 'Asherim' (the wooden poles of the goddess Asherah) + ḥammānîm 'sun-pillars'
entries.literal: all the stones of the altar like chalkstones shattered; Asherim and sun-pillars shall not stand
entries.standardEnglish: all the stones of the altar as chalkstones that are beaten in sunder, so that the Asherim and the sun-images shall rise no more (ASV); no Asherim or sun-images shall stand (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'when he makes all the altar-stones like crushed chalkstones, no Asherim or sun-pillars shall stand' — ʾăšērîm transliterated 'Asherim' (the wooden cult-poles; the goddess Asherah / Ugaritic ʾAṯiratu link carried in commentary, the central athirat-asherah entry deliberately NOT applied — the referent is the cult-object, not the goddess); ḥammānîm 'sun-pillars' (with NJPS 'incense-altars' noted). The kpr 'atoned for' of the same verse is governed by the overlay kupar-atonement-isaiah (appliesTo extended to ISA-27:9); ʿăwōn 'iniquity' by the central avon-iniquity-cross-corpus-keyword (extended to ISA-27:9).
entries.rationale: The condition of the atonement of 27:9 is the demolition of the cult: 'when he makes all the altar-stones (ʾaḇnê mizbēaḥ) like crushed chalkstones (kᵉ-ʾaḇnê-ḡir mᵉnuppāṣôṯ; gir 'chalk, lime', nāp̄aṣ 'shatter'), Asherim and sun-pillars shall not stand.' Two lexical decisions. (i) ʾăšērîm (H842) are the wooden cult-poles of the goddess Asherah — the Hebrew reflex, by the regular ṯ->š shift, of Ugaritic ʾAṯiratu (ʾaṯrt), ʾIlu's consort and mother of the gods (central athirat-asherah-mother-goddess-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible). The translation transliterates 'Asherim' (with 'Asherah-poles / sacred poles' as equivalents), the standard rendering; the central athirat-asherah entry is deliberately NOT applied to ISA-27:9, because its wohChoice is the Ugaritic goddess proper-name 'ʾAṯiratu' and the referent at 27:9 is the cult-OBJECT (the pole being demolished), not the goddess herself — a referent/rendering mismatch of the same kind that governs the yamm (deified Sea vs common-noun sea) and rephaim (giants vs shades) non-extensions. The goddess/pole cross-corpus link is documented here and in commentary, not asserted by an appliesTo extension. (ii) ḥammānîm (H2553) are rendered 'sun-pillars / sun-images' (the standard value, the cultic stelae associated with sun-worship), with the NJPS 'incense-altars' noted as the live alternative. The renderings are standard and carry no lens (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39; BDB, HALOT s.v. ʾăšērāh, ḥammān).

entries.translit: ʿîr bᵉṣûrāh bāḏāḏ … kî lō ʿam-bînôṯ hû … ʿōśēhû … wᵉ-yōṣᵉrô
entries.strongs: H5892 (ʿîr 'city'); H1219 (bāṣar 'fortify'); H909 (bāḏāḏ 'alone, solitary'); H998 (bînāh 'understanding'); H6213 (ʿāśāh 'make'); H3335 (yāṣar 'form, fashion')
entries.lemma: the unnamed ʿîr bᵉṣûrāh 'fortified city' left solitary (27:10) + the withered harvest, the ʿam-bînôṯ 'people without understanding', and its ʿōśēhû 'Maker' / yōṣᵉrô 'Fashioner' (27:11)
entries.partOfSpeech: noun-phrase (unnamed city) + verbal clauses + two divine-epithet participles
entries.literal: for the fortified city is solitary … for it is not a people of understanding; therefore its Maker will not pity it, and its Fashioner will not favor it
entries.standardEnglish: For the fortified city is solitary … it is a people of no understanding; therefore he that made them will not have compassion upon them, and he that formed them will show them no favor (ASV/JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'the fortified city is solitary … it is a people without understanding; therefore its Maker will not have compassion on it, and its Fashioner will not be gracious to it' — the city left UNNAMED, its referent (a foreign / enemy capital vs Jerusalem itself under judgment) unresolved in the line and weighed only in commentary; ʿōśēhû / yōṣᵉrô 'its Maker' / 'its Fashioner' (the creation-verbs ʿśh 'make' and yṣr 'form, fashion').
entries.rationale: 27:10-11 describe an unnamed ʿîr bᵉṣûrāh 'fortified city' (bāṣar 'cut off, make inaccessible, fortify') left bāḏāḏ 'solitary, alone', a forsaken pasture where the calf grazes and strips the branches (27:10); when its harvest (qāṣîr) dries up the boughs are broken and women come to kindle them, 'for it is a people without understanding (ʿam-bînôṯ), therefore its Maker (ʿōśēhû, ʿśh) will not have compassion on it and its Fashioner (yōṣᵉrô, yṣr) will not be gracious to it' (27:11). The renderings are standard; the one flagged point is that the city is deliberately left UNNAMED, and its referent is a scholarly crux — a foreign or enemy capital (a Samaria-, Moab-, or generic-oppressor city, the counterpart to the strong city of salvation in 26:1) versus Jerusalem itself under judgment. The translation renders the city plainly and does not resolve the identification in the line, leaving it for commentary (accuracy-before-lens). ʿōśēhû 'its Maker' and yōṣᵉrô 'its Fashioner' are the two creation-participles applied to the people; they are rendered by their standard values and receive no lens. The renderings are standard (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39; Kaiser, Isaiah 13-39, OTL).

entries.translit: yaḥbōṭ YHWH miš-šibbōleṯ han-nāhār ʿaḏ-naḥal miṣrāyim wᵉ-ʾattem tᵉluqqᵉṭû lᵉ-ʾaḥaḏ ʾeḥāḏ
entries.strongs: H2251 (ḥāḇaṭ 'beat off, thresh'); H7641 (šibbōleṯ 'ear of grain; flowing stream'); H5104 (nāhār 'river'); H5158 (naḥal 'wadi, brook'); H3950 (lāqaṭ 'glean, gather up')
entries.lemma: yaḥbōṭ 'beat off / thresh' (unexpressed object) + the šibbōleṯ 'flowing stream' / 'ear of grain' pun + han-nāhār 'the River' (Euphrates) / naḥal miṣrayim 'the Wadi of Egypt' (the idealized N-S boundaries) + tᵉluqqᵉṭû lᵉ-ʾaḥaḏ ʾeḥāḏ 'gathered one by one'
entries.literal: YHWH will beat off from the flowing stream of the River to the Wadi of Egypt, and you shall be gleaned one by one
entries.standardEnglish: Jehovah will beat off his fruit from the flood of the River unto the brook of Egypt; and ye shall be gathered one by one (ASV); the LORD will beat off [His fruit] from the flood of the River unto the Brook of Egypt (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'YHWH will beat off the grain, from the flowing stream of the River to the Wadi of Egypt, and you shall be gathered up one by one' — the unexpressed object of yaḥbōṭ supplied as 'the grain' (JPS supplies '[His fruit]'); šibbōleṯ 'flowing stream' (with the 'ear of grain' pun on the threshing-verb flagged); han-nāhār = the Euphrates, naḥal miṣrayim = the Wadi of Egypt (the southern boundary); tᵉluqqᵉṭû lᵉ-ʾaḥaḏ ʾeḥāḏ 'gathered up one by one', the eschatological ingathering.
entries.rationale: 27:12 opens the ingathering. yaḥbōṭ (ḥbṭ 'beat off, thresh', as one beats olives or grain from the tree or stalk, cf. Deut 24:20; Ruth 2:17) has an unexpressed object; the translation supplies 'the grain' (JPS supplies '[His fruit]'), and the verb governs the harvest-imagery of the whole verse. šibbōleṯ ha-nāhār is a deliberate pun: šibbōleṯ means both 'flowing stream, channel, flood' (so 'the flowing stream of the River', JPS 'the flood of the River') AND 'ear of grain', resonating with the threshing-verb — the translation renders 'flowing stream' and flags the grain-pun. han-nāhār 'the River' is the Euphrates and naḥal miṣrayim 'the Wadi of Egypt' (Wadi el-ʿArish) is the southern boundary — together the idealized north-south extent of the land from which Israel is gathered. tᵉluqqᵉṭû (lqṭ 'glean, gather up') lᵉ-ʾaḥaḏ ʾeḥāḏ 'you shall be gathered up one by one' completes the harvest-and-gleaning image of the eschatological gathering of Israel. The renderings are standard and carry no lens; the entry records the supplied object, the šibbōleṯ pun, and the boundary-toponyms (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39; BDB, HALOT s.v. šibbōleṯ).

entries.source: יִתָּקַע בְּשׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל וּבָאוּ הָאֹבְדִים בְּאֶרֶץ אַשּׁוּר וְהַנִּדָּחִים בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם וְהִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לַיהוָה
entries.translit: yittāqaʿ bᵉ-šôp̄ār gāḏôl û-ḇāʾû hā-ʾōḇᵉḏîm bᵉ-ʾereṣ ʾaššûr wᵉ-han-niddāḥîm bᵉ-ʾereṣ miṣrāyim wᵉ-hištaḥăwû la-YHWH
entries.strongs: H8628 (tāqaʿ 'blow, thrust'); H7782 (šôp̄ār 'ram's-horn, trumpet'); H6 (ʾāḇaḏ 'perish, be lost'); H5080 (nāḏaḥ 'drive away, banish'); H7812 (šāḥāh / ḥwh 'bow down, do obeisance, worship')
entries.lemma: šôp̄ār gāḏôl 'a great trumpet' (blown, Niphal yittāqaʿ) + hā-ʾōḇᵉḏîm 'those perishing / the lost' (in Assyria) / han-niddāḥîm 'the driven-out / outcast' (in Egypt) + hištaḥăwû 'they shall bow down' (cultic worship of YHWH)
entries.partOfSpeech: noun (trumpet) + two substantival participles (the lost / the outcast) + verb (worship)
entries.literal: a great trumpet shall be blown, and those perishing in the land of Assyria and those driven out in the land of Egypt shall come, and they shall bow down to YHWH
entries.standardEnglish: a great trumpet shall be blown; and they shall come that were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and they that were outcasts in the land of Egypt; and they shall worship Jehovah (ASV); a great horn shall be blown (JPS)
entries.wohChoice: 'a great trumpet shall be blown, and those perishing in the land of Assyria and those driven out in the land of Egypt shall come, and they shall bow down to YHWH on the holy mountain in Jerusalem' — šôp̄ār 'trumpet' (the ram's-horn; JPS 'horn'; the transliteration 'shofar' marks the cultic register); hā-ʾōḇᵉḏîm 'those perishing / the lost', han-niddāḥîm 'those driven out / the outcast'; hištaḥăwû 'bow down' in the cultic-worship register of YHWH — the central hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship entry (wohChoice 'made obeisance', the human-homage register) deliberately NOT applied. The eschatological ingathering carried in commentary.
entries.rationale: The chapter's climax: yittāqaʿ bᵉ-šôp̄ār gāḏôl 'a great trumpet shall be blown' (yittāqaʿ, Niphal of tqʿ 'blow'; šôp̄ār, the ram's-horn) summons hā-ʾōḇᵉḏîm 'those perishing / the lost ones' (ʾbd) in the land of Assyria and han-niddāḥîm 'the driven-out / outcast / dispersed' (ndḥ) in the land of Egypt to come and hištaḥăwû 'bow down' to YHWH on the holy mountain (har ha-qōḏeš) at Jerusalem. Four decisions, all standard. (i) šôp̄ār gāḏôl is 'a great trumpet' (the ram's-horn; JPS 'a great horn'; the transliteration 'shofar' is noted for the cultic register); no central or overlay šôp̄ār entry previously existed. (ii) hā-ʾōḇᵉḏîm 'those perishing / the lost' and han-niddāḥîm 'those driven out / the outcast / dispersed' are the two groups of exiles, rendered by their standard values. (iii) hištaḥăwû (Hishtaphel of ḥwh, H7812) is here cultic worship of the deity — 'bow down / worship' YHWH — a different register from the human-homage 'made obeisance' of the central hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship entry (scoped to the Genesis Yosef-cycle, wohChoice 'made obeisance'); that entry is deliberately NOT applied to ISA-27:13, since the referent here is worship of YHWH, not homage to a human superior — a register mismatch of the kind recorded for the elohim, refaim, and yamm non-extensions. The translation renders 'bow down' (with 'worship' as the cultic equivalent). (iv) the toponyms Aššûr (Assyria), Miṣrayim (Egypt), and Yᵉrûšālāim (Jerusalem) are standard. The great-trumpet ingathering of the lost and the outcast is the eschatological gathering-of-the-dispersed, developed in commentary (cf. Matt 24:31); the renderings are standard and carry no lens (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39; BDB, HALOT s.v. šôp̄ār, nāḏaḥ).
